title: feat(app): diagnostics and transport compatibility wave (#451, #514, #540-#542, #544, #546, #550-#551, #556)
body:
# feat(app): diagnostics and transport compatibility wave (#451, #514, #540–#542, #544, #546, #550–#551, #556)

Branch: `zl-diagnostics-transport-wave-a` · 11 commits · 57 files, +4765/−247 · +109 tests
Baseline: 1713 collectable tests green → **1822 green** (the only failures, before and after, are the 11 wasm-glue
tests that collect only where CI generates `app/src/rewriter_wasm/`; `tsc --noEmit` shows only that same
pre-existing import error in this environment).

Advances ten open issues in one wave, following the wave-A pattern: every behavior change is test-verified,
every limitation is documented honestly, and nothing pretends to be more than it is. Scope decisions were made
conservatively — where an issue asks for a design or a policy, this wave delivers exactly that and no invented
code.

## Per-commit summary

### 1. `fix(app): capability reporting and honest docs for WebRTC and plaintext WebSockets (#544)`
- `zl:ping` now answers with a factual `capabilities` object: `websocket` (native-bridge/relay),
  `websocketPlaintext` (true since #525), `webrtc: "unavailable"`, `replaySpool`. Hosts and sites can finally
  tell unavailable from broken.
- **Docs debt fixed**: `docs/websocket.md`, `docs/security.md`, the `wsidentity.ts` header and several e2e
  comments still claimed "ws:// is upgraded to wss://" — behavior that #525 removed. All rewritten to the actual
  pass-through contract, plus an explicit WebRTC-unavailable section (RTCPeerConnection is deleted in navguard;
  exact failure mode: constructor absence, no silent fallback, and why — ICE egress bypasses the engine).

### 2. `fix(app): native-parity WebSocket.url and drain-aware bufferedAmount contract (#546)`
- The page shim's `url` property is pinned to the WHATWG constructor contract (resolution, http(s)→ws(s),
  fragment refusal) and tested for relative/ws/wss/http/https inputs; the engine side keeps logging only the
  engine-origin identity, so nothing new leaks anywhere.
- `WsHandle` gains an optional `drainAt(): number | null` seam (mirroring `ping()`/`lastPongAt()`). The vendored
  transports expose no write-acceptance today, so the wisp factory leaves it unset and behavior is unchanged;
  the relay gets no fake drain frame (documented as bridge-queue-accounted). `docs/websocket.md` gains an
  "Observable semantics" subsection that states exactly what `bufferedAmount` is and is not.

### 3. `feat(app): close the large-streamed-body redirect replay gap (#556)`
- Gap analysis found the OPFS spool machinery already on main but gated behind a default-off `spoolUploads`
  host flag — so the default behavior still surfaced a mapped-Location one-shot response for >32 MiB bodies.
- The spool path was already bounded and honestly failable (256 MiB/512 MiB budgets, pre-byte fallback with
  diagnostics), so the fix is the **documented default flip**: over-cap redirects now replay through the spool
  by default; `zl:config spoolUploads:false` opts out.
- Known operational consequence, stated plainly: unannounced streamed bodies also prefer the spool path by
  design (that is pre-existing, CI-verified behavior) — page POSTs now generally take the OPFS route.
- Exact Fetch redirect semantics untouched: 301/302/303 conversion, 307/308 preservation, cross-origin header
  stripping, 10-hop cap, no removed caps.

### 4. `fix(app): redirect-torture failure diagnostics and 307/308 re-issue hardening (#514)`
- **Honest status: diagnosed, not fixed.** The audit of the re-issue path found the re-fetches correctly share
  one buffered/spooled body and the wedge-guard cannot double-fire — no defect explaining the intermittent CI
  failure. `docs/transport-lifecycle.md` says exactly that.
- One **concrete defect found and fixed**: when `spoolTransportCopy` threw, the spool `release()` rode a
  statement after the `await` and never ran — stranding the spool file and up to 256 MiB of budget until the
  orphan sweep. Release now rides the same `finally` as the copy.
- The torture probe now records `failedCode` and the full `zeolite: upstream fetch failed: …` suffix (bounded)
  in its JSON contract instead of dying in a `SyntaxError`, and re-issue hop failures emit a bounded
  `UPSTREAM`/`REDIRECT_HOP` warning naming hop index and redirecting status — the next red run will name its
  cause.

### 5. `feat(app): bounded per-attempt CAPTCHA tracing with redacted stages (#451)`
- New bounded ring (`captcha-trace.ts`, ≤64 attempts × ≤16 stage records, overwrite-oldest, drop counters):
  `BOOTSTRAP_SEEN / ASSET_LOAD / FRAME_HANDSHAKE / SUBMISSION / VERIFY_OUTCOME` with the HTTP outcome class,
  transport route and timing; unobservable stages are recorded `unknown`, never guessed. Provider class comes
  only from URL classification, pinned in a test against `isChallengeFrameUrl` so the two cannot drift.
- Hooked into the six existing `CHALLENGE` emit sites (2–4 lines each, no new interception). Widget-internal
  verify calls the engine never sees stay unrecorded — documented as "not a pass", per the no-bypass rule.
- Exposed host-only via a new `zl:captchaTrace` control message (dispatch + `CORE_CONTROL_TYPES` registry pin).
- Records are redacted (`redactSecrets` on entry), and a test feeds hostile URLs to prove no
  `g-recaptcha-response` / `h-captcha-response` / `cf-turnstile-response` substrings survive; a test proves two
  concurrent clientIds never mix attempts.
- Not in this commit: real-browser direct-vs-proxied fixtures (CI/Playwright work — listed below), KDL report
  extension.

### 6. `feat(app): consistent fixed-offset timezone identity and fingerprint surface inventory (#540)`
- The profile contract is **narrowed to a self-consistent fixed offset**, expressed through real IANA zones so
  Date and Intl agree everywhere: offset→`Etc/GMT±N` (sign-inverted, as IANA defines), `Etc/GMT` for UTC,
  offset-string fallback (`+05:30`) for half-hours and west of `Etc/GMT+12` (which IANA does not define — a real
  gap handled rather than faked). `Date.prototype.toString`/`toTimeString` zone text is formatted from the
  offset in Chromium's Etc shape; deterministic across repeated reads; `toJSON` stays UTC-ISO (real-Chromium
  parity, asserted).
- Worker script gets identical treatment (shared extracted builders). An explicit `timezoneName` still wins;
  an Etc name contradicting `utcOffsetMin` is recorded (`timezoneInconsistent`), never silently rewritten.
- A test pins the narrowed contract at a real America/New_York spring-forward instant: the named zone shifts,
  the Etc path does not — that is the promise now.
- New versioned inventory `docs/fingerprint-surfaces.md` (`schemaVersion: 1`): every controlled surface with
  page/worker scope, test file and honest status; fonts/timing/TLS listed as explicitly native/transport-owned.
  `docs/fingerprint.md` "Honest limits" rewritten to match.

### 7. `feat(app): persist extension download handoff across worker restarts (#541)`
- The extension `downloads.download()` handoff registry is now write-through to IndexedDB (extensions DB
  v4→v5, new `download-handoffs` store; the engine's own stores are untouched and the upgrade test proves v4
  data survives) and rehydrates on background boot with a `recoveredAt` marker.
- Honest reconciliation: terminal states are final — no resurrection, no double-completion when the host
  re-reports, one bounded diagnostic per re-report; records the host never finishes stay at their last known
  non-terminal state (the engine cannot distinguish cancel/tab-close/silent-host and does not guess);
  7-day retention drops stale records. A storage failure is a bounded diagnostic, never a failed handoff
  (and a cached-IDB-rejection wedge found on the way is fixed).
- No file bytes persisted; `docs/downloads.md` documents the retention contract and the unknowable cases.

### 8. `feat(app): cosmetic CSS selector injection from Ghostery lists — first slice (#551)`
- The styles arm of `@ghostery/adblocker` 2.20.1 `getCosmeticsFilters` now applies to document responses, on
  the same enablement path as network blocking (host toggle, per-site override, shipped captcha/anti-bot
  allowlist as the single source of truth), injected via the existing after-doctype splice (64 KiB cap,
  `</style`-escape neutralized).
- One bounded diagnostic per document: applied / exception-suppressed / unsupported counts, aggregates only.
  Scriptlets and extended/HTML filters are counted and never executed; generic DOM-anchored hides are
  documented as not applicable at rewrite time.
- `docs/interception.md` now says precisely what cosmetic coverage is and is not — still explicitly **not**
  full EasyList/Ghostery compatibility.

### 9. `feat(app): Tier 2 DOM inspection bridge — first slice, host-gated (#550)`
- postMessage-only content bridge (serialized data, never DOM objects) + engine half + a minimal DevTools
  panel. **Default OFF**: the devtools page authorizes per live proxied client; senders are host-gated.
- Bounded and redacted: snapshot depth 12 / 500 nodes with counted truncation, computed styles capped at 64,
  console ring 128 × 8 args × 500 chars with objects flattened to class names; `.value` is never read and
  sensitive attributes never serialized; the engine side re-runs the authoritative `redactSecrets`.
- Navigation invalidation via a generation stamp (netlog pattern): both ends discard stale generations, so a
  stale DevTools page cannot inspect a later document.
- Not in this slice: element highlighting, the storage view, and the spec's strict-privacy-mode toggle (none
  exists; the gate is purely the explicit per-session authorization) — documented as not shipped.

### 10. `docs(app): signed engine module system design and threat model (#542)`
- The 7.0 Erionite row finally has its design: `docs/plugin-modules-design.md`. Centered on the constraint the
  runtime actually imposes — no dynamic `import()` and no eval in the SW scope, so signed modules are
  **verified bundle bindings** (attribution, integrity, revocation), not late loading, and the document says so.
  Ed25519 manifest format, typed permissions extending the power-features vocabulary, the stream-hook contract
  (backpressure, deadlines, quotas, strikes, fault isolation), the threat model, migration path, open questions.
  `docs/plugins.md` and the roadmap row point at it, marked design-only.

### 11. `docs(agents)` — AGENTS.md version-log record for the wave.

## Test coverage added (new/extended files, +109 tests)
`captcha-trace.test.ts` (17) · `fingerprint.test.ts` (+13) · downloads handoff persistence (11, incl. the v4→v5
upgrade survival test) · `cosmetic-injection.test.ts` (17) · `dom-inspect.test.ts` (20) · `capability.test.ts` ·
`wsbridge.test.ts` (drainAt describe) · `ws-shim.test.ts` (url parity) · `replay-body.test.ts` (over-cap 307/308
two-hop SHA-256 chains, spool fallback, bounded warnings) · `bodyspool.test.ts` (mid-spool source death) ·
`transform.test.ts` (+3 cosmetic splice tests).

## Deliberately not in this wave
- **#514 root cause**: no defect explaining the intermittent CI failure was found; this wave ships the
  diagnostics that will name it (§4 above) and fixes a real spool-release leak found during the audit.
- **#451 real-browser fixtures** (direct-vs-proxied reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile) — CI/Playwright work,
  needs the e2e runner budget; the unit-level stage/redaction/isolation acceptance is complete.
- **#551 scriptlets, extended selectors, dynamic-mutation re-injection** and **#550 highlighting/storage
  view/strict-mode toggle** — explicitly out of the first slices, documented in the docs this wave updated.
- **#542 implementation** — the issue is a design item; this wave delivers the design only.
- No wasm-seam changes; no bootstrap-budget changes (the bridge adds a measured +2,985 bytes; the pre-existing
  main-vs-documented budget drift is unchanged and noted for CI).

title: Troubleshooting a 404 error on a Netlify site
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/polaris111/agent-runs/6ae77d72e9938288e084e5f5

🤖 **Agent:** Claude (claude-opus-5)

💬 **Prompt:** The site says Page not found
Looks like you’ve followed a broken link or entered a URL that doesn’t exist on this site.

If this is your site, and you weren’t expecting a 404 for this path, please visit Netlify’s “page not found” support guide for tr...

✅ **Result:**

The deployed site was returning Netlify's "Page not found" placeholder for every
URL, including the homepage. Polaris was written as an Express application: a
long-running Node server rendered each page on request, exposed a small `/api`,
and proxied game assets. Nothing in the repository told Netlify what to publish,
so the deploy contained no pages at all. Polaris now builds into a static site
that Netlify can serve, with the handful of genuinely dynamic pieces moved onto
Netlify primitives.

## Build

A new build step renders the site ahead of time. It injects the partials from
`templates/` (navbar, sidebar, meta tags, analytics) into every page, the job the
server previously did on each request, and it copies the Ultraviolet, epoxy and
bare-mux client files out of `node_modules` so the proxy front end is served from
the site rather than resolved at runtime. The `/api/games`, `/api/apps`,
`/api/cheats` and `/api/changelog` responses are generated as JSON files from the
same source data the server read, keeping the shape the front end expects. Build
configuration lives in `netlify.toml`, and the build is also available locally as
`npm run build:static`.

## Request-time pieces

Game assets under `/cdn` are fetched by an edge function. A plain proxy was not
enough here: the upstream asset host labels every file as plain text, which would
make game pages render as source instead of running, so the edge function sets
the content type from the file extension the way the Express route used to. It
also re-adds the small script that hides a game page when somebody opens it
directly rather than through the player. The favicon lookup used by the tab
cloaking settings became a function at the same path, `/api/favicon`. Unknown
URLs now land on Polaris' own 404 page instead of Netlify's.

## Fixes found along the way

Several things were broken independently of hosting and would have kept the site
from working once it loaded:

- Every game click stalled on the player page. It waited on `/baremux/bare.cjs`,
  a filename bare-mux stopped shipping after 2.0, and the script loader never
  settled when a file was missing. The loader now reports failures, the real
  filename is used, and proxy setup was rewritten against the current bare-mux
  API. Games served from this origin no longer wait on proxy setup at all.
- The default proxy transport was `libcurl`, which the client has no support for,
  so starting the player threw before it could load anything. It now defaults to
  epoxy, the only transport the settings menu offers.
- A typo in the homepage changelog sizing code threw on every visit.
- When analytics was unreachable, the failure path fell through and crashed on
  undefined data instead of quietly disabling itself.
- The player page opened with a leftover debug alert on every game load, telling
  users to reload if they saw the bare-client error that is now fixed.

## One limitation

The proxy tunnels through a `/wisp/` websocket endpoint, and Netlify cannot
accept the websocket upgrade that requires. The large majority of the catalog is
hosted under `/cdn` and does not use the proxy, so those games work on the
deployed site; loading an external site through the proxy does not. The wisp
endpoint is now configurable rather than hardcoded to the site's own origin, so
pointing the deploy at a wisp server running elsewhere is a matter of setting the
`POLARIS_WISP_URL` environment variable, for example
`wss://wisp.example.com/wisp/`. This is documented in the README.

title: The world, the loot, the kits, the errands, the events, the atlas, the world on the server, a world boss and notes: solo and co-op play
body:
## What was built

This branch grew in one cloud session, piece by piece, each with its tests (Robin, 2026-10-31: keep developing in the cloud before it goes local). Everything is inside `Game Developer/`; the brief and `CLAUDE.md` are untouched. The first eleven commits built an island, a camera, landings, a first fight, a character screen and a shop; **the twelfth replaced the island with the world Robin described on 2026-10-31**; then **a balance pass from bots, a second pass over the screen and the server's world tick**; then **the world grows**: areas generated by tier beyond the Summit, without end (Robin: "Do it"); then **the loot, the kits and the enemies worth reading** (Robin, the evening of 2026-10-31: unique weapons and trinkets that change how you play, bosses that drop the good things, abilities that make the classes feel different; then the whole list in my order); then **the towns' errands, the trainer, flasks that scale and a bag that fills**; then **the themes' events, locked vaults, two more shapes, the world as a list, culling, the first minutes and the settings**; then **the world on the server: the protocol written first, accounts, the client over the socket, two phones in one world**; and **the last gives that world its first shared things: a world boss everyone fights together, and notes left on spots**. This description covers the result.

**Robin's decisions** are written down in `docs/decisions-2026-10-31.md` for the local session to merge into the brief: one big map in themed areas by tier; mobs in their own parts; normal spots with the area's creatures and sometimes a chest, a merchant, a gambler or a mini-boss; chests, springs and shrines as special spots; bosses on the board at the passage to the next area, beaten by landing exactly on them, back five minutes later; randomized tiered gear with ranks and named versions, five slots, a simple bag; a turn-based RPG fight with a defensive choice; mana for everyone; anyone can charge; classes with a kit that grows; no town liberation; death to the nearest town for a fifth of the gold; the working title Zite. Every number and layout is mine, first settings, marked so in the docs.

### The world (rules)
`rules/data/world.json`: three hand-laid areas, **Ashford Meadows** (tier 1, levels 1 to 4), **Thornwood** (2, 4 to 8), **Frostpeak** (3, 8 to 12), 187 spots, each area with a town, a shop, a shrine, chests, springs and mostly wilds; the **Iron Gate** (Thornwood Warden) opens Thornwood, the **Briar Gate** (Briar King) opens Frostpeak, the **Summit** (Frost Matriarch, now in Frostpeak's north-east corner) opens the first grown area. The road beyond a gate belongs to the next area and is closed until its boss falls. `docs/state/world.md` has the layout, the mobs and the rules the layout passes.

### The world grows (rules, `rules/src/generate.ts`, `rules/data/themes.json`)
When the boss at the end of the last area falls, the next area is laid **from the world's seed and its number alone**, so every client and the server lay the same one. Gen-n is **tier 3 + n**, levels 4·tier − 4 to 4·tier, its theme the n-th of eight (fire, water, swamp, desert, crystal, shadow, sky, jungle) round and round with a new name each round (Emberfall, Mistwater, Murkfen, Sunscar, Glimmerdeep, Duskmoor, Skyreach, Verdant Tangle, Ashen Reach, …). The cells (1400 by 1900) snake east from the third column, two rows tall; the board widens as they come. The shape is one of the hand-laid areas re-dressed: a way in ("Emberfall Pass", plain wilds) judged by whether the passage from the opener can reach it without cutting another road, a way out (a "<Adjective> Gate" with the area's boss, opening gen-n+1), the kinds kept and then a town, a shop, a shrine, two chests and two springs made sure of, hubs named from the theme. Its creatures go on the board's **bestiary**: four mobs of the theme in four shapes, a mini-boss and a boss, Frostpeak's numbers grown a tier at a time (HP ×1.25, attack ×1.15, defense ×1.12, xp and gold ×1.3; set by the bots' walls). Gear ranks run past the ten names (Copper … Sunmetal, then "Rank 11"), a rank's number ×1.35 and its price ×1.8 beyond the tables; the xp table reaches level 30. The passage from the opener is laid as wilds a step apart, bowed as little as needed so every spot keeps clear of every other. Hints name the area beyond a gate by peeking before it is laid. **State version 6**; a version-5 save is brought up by laying its opened areas again.

### Loot worth talking about (rules, `rules/data/uniques.json`)
**Uniques**: 23 named pieces, each with a power the rules read by name: Twinfang strikes twice, Quickdraw crits first and holds the enemy back a round, Frostbrand chills, Venomtooth poisons, Mindshard halves mana costs, Gorefang grows as HP is missing, Stormcaller crits every third hit, the Sunblade hits bosses harder; Wardweave turns the first wound-up blow aside, Mirrormail throws back half of what you block, Thornhide softens blows under half HP; the Phoenix Helm catches a fall once a fight, the Sage's Crown adds half the xp, Ironbrow shrugs off poison, weakening and crits; Striders turn a one into a two, Windstep starts every fight with a step aside, Pathfinders halve a spot's wait; the Miser's Coin doubles gold and halves xp, the Heartstone heals every round, the Sapphire Tear gives mana, the Lucky Charm re-rolls the die (a Charm chip), the Phoenix Feather raises the fallen once every half hour, the Wolf Totem feeds the meter. A rarity of their own, never rolled by chance. **Bosses drop the good things**: a unique half the time and never under epic; minis rare and up with a unique in ten; legendaries carry two affixes. `describeGear` says what a unique does, in orange on the screen.

### Class kits that feel different (rules, `rules/data/abilities.json`, `classes.json`)
Each class builds a **meter**: the Warrior's **Rage** from blows taken (two from a wound-up one), the Rogue's **Combo** from hits landed, the Mage's **Flow** a point a round, the Ranger's **Focus** from blows that miss it and crits. Six abilities a class now, three new each: **Execute** (3 Rage, far harder on a foe under a third), **Rally** (heal and hit harder), **Shield Wall**; **Smoke Bomb** (3 Combo: the next blow misses, the next hit a sure crit), **Pickpocket** (gold from the purse, once a fight), **Eviscerate** (all the Combo); **Time Warp** (4 Flow: the enemy loses its turn, boss or not), **Meteor** (lands two rounds later whatever you do), **Mana Shield** (all your mana into a barrier); **Trap** (the next wind-up fails), **Hawk** (strikes on its own each round), **Mark** (the next hits harder). **Levels 4, 8, 12, … offer a pick of one ability in two** in the chip row, so two characters of a class grow apart; shrines teach the rest.

### Enemies worth reading (rules, `rules/data/enemies.json`, `themes.json`)
**The enemy tells its next move a round ahead** (the fight screen's status leads with it: "next: Venom Bite (poison)", "next: Smash lands, hard. Block it!"), so the guard is chosen for something. Moves carry **effects**: spiders and the Warden's thorns poison, wisps and wraiths drain mana, golems harden, wraiths fade, treants regrow, wolves and yetis weaken. **Bosses have a second phase under half HP** with a line and new moves (the Warden's bark splits, the Briar King regrows, the Matriarch's heart freezes over; grown bosses rage in their theme's way). Hand-laid bosses and minis carry a tenth more HP. State version 7, a migration from 6.

### Errands, the trainer, the flasks and the bag (rules, `rules/data/quests.json`, `rules/src/quests.ts`)
**Towns give errands**: walk into a town with none from it and it asks one in the chip row (Take it, Not now): thin a creature of the area, open chests in it, hunt its mini-boss, or bring down its boss. Progress counts wherever it happens; back in town it pays gold and xp by the tier, a hunt or a boss sometimes a unique; three carried at most, one a town; the town's hint says how it stands. **The trainer** in a town's shop (a Train tab) teaches an ability of the class for the tier's price and raises ranks for more (Robin: skills are bought, found or earned). **The potion heals four tenths of max HP** and a **mana potion** gives half the mana back, so flasks keep up with the tiers; springs give one of each. **The bag holds twelve**: a piece with no room asks to be sold for half or left, buying gear is refused until there is room. A level's pick now waits its turn (`picks`) instead of blocking the other questions. State version 8, migrations from 7 and the chain below.

### Events, vaults and shapes (rules, `rules/data/events.json`, `shapes.json`)
**A wild spot now and then holds the theme's event**: the meadows' picnic heals, Thornwood's brambles and Frostpeak's cold bite, lava burns, the tide pays, the swamp's wisp hands a flask, the crystals clear the mind, the storm throws a card; a hurt never takes the last point. **Two more shapes** join the three hand-laid areas as what the generator dresses (the ladder, the wheel), each with a **locked vault**: it opens only with the area's key, which the area's mini-boss drops once, and holds three times the gold, a piece never under epic and a unique three times in ten; the vault's hint says who carries the key. State version 9.

### The world on the server (`docs/state/protocol.md`, `server/`, `client/src/remote-game.ts`)
**The protocol was written before the networking** (the skill shared-world, rule 8): join, intent, snapshot, result, event, leave, ping; every message's fields, who sends it and what answers it; the delta; reconnecting; the limits. **The rules** gained `join` (a character at the start for a new account), `newWorld` (nobody in it yet), `diffState`/`mergeDelta` (what an action changed, by reference) and the protocol's types, shared by both sides; a test plays two bots six hundred actions and checks a client folding every delta ends with exactly the server's state. **The server**: schema 2 with accounts (a token per device, a recovery code per character such as `KPM4-R7QX-2HJD`), the `Hub` in front of the region actor: join with a token, a code or a name and a class; intents stamped with the account's id whatever the client wrote, answered with their delta, what others did bundled every 60 ms into one event; who is online; 30 intents in 10 s and a flood cut off; the actor's answers carry the delta; old answers forgotten after three days. **The client**: one interface for the holder of the state, the local game and the remote one behind it, every intent a promise, one in flight at a time; `?server=wss://…` once and remembered; the character screen makes the account; a connect screen that never stops trying, with Play offline meanwhile and Start over when the account is gone; the other players on the board as marks with their names (dim when offline), "with Bo" in the place line, a line when someone joins, opens an area, beats a boss, levels or falls; the link under the die (solo, online · 2 here, reconnecting); the settings show the world, the account's code, Use a code and Start over. A dead socket is replaced on `visibilitychange`, `pageshow` and the minute's tick; the intent in flight is sent again with its id after the snapshot. **The save is the account**: the solo save stays for offline play; the server never takes a state from a client. Token and code are stored plain on Robin's PC (hashing is a step for a public server). One region holds the world today.

### The world boss and the notes (rules, `rules/test/coop.test.ts`)
**A world boss** (mine; item 16 of Robin's list): now and then a tick brings the boss of the highest area anyone has opened onto a wild spot there, with two and a half times its HP, for half an hour. Everyone who lands there fights the same beast: a round reads the HP from the spawn and writes it back, the damage tallied by player; when it falls everyone in the tally is paid by their share (never under a quarter) with a boss's drop roll each (a unique half the time), and the others' fights on it end in the same action; when its time is up it leaves and lets the fighters go. On the board it is a big purple W with its HP above it; the fight screen says "world boss", follows the shared HP when others hit it, and ends with your share when someone else lands the last blow. The gate bosses stay each player's own (each opens their own way); whether an area should open for everyone once anyone beat its boss is Robin's call (the idea bank). **Notes**: a tap on the spot you stand on offers four set lines as chips ("Danger!", "Loot here", "Boss near", "Help!"); the note sits on the spot (a small mark; one a player a spot, three a spot, gone after a day) and every hint on that spot ends with who left what and when; the others hear "Anna left a note at …". State version 10 (`traces`), a migration from 9.

### What happens on the board (rules)
A town rests you, and has an errand and a trainer. A chest gives gold and maybe gear, then empties for five minutes; a spring a potion, three; a shrine a new ability of your class or a rank for one, ten. The wilds roll a fight with the area's creatures (70 in 100), a chest, a wandering merchant, a gambler (double or nothing on a die, high or low) or a mini-boss. Landing exactly on a boss spot starts its fight. A `tick` once a minute (the page's, and the server's) lets a mini-boss or a merchant spawn on a wild spot of an open area for ten minutes. Tapping any spot gives a hint: the area and its levels, what roams there, what a chest or boss holds, never what a wild spot holds this time.

### Gear and the bag (rules)
Ranks by tier, rarities common to legendary by weight, one rolled number per piece, an affix from rare up (crit, lifesteal, dodge, thorns, vigor), a proper name from epic up ("Stormborn, iron sword"). Shops sell the plain piece of their area's rank for each slot and the potion and dice cards, and buy back at half. Equip, unequip, drop; `stats` adds what is worn.

### The fight (rules)
One intent a round: **a move** (Attack, an ability with its mana cost, Charge for a double hit, a Potion, Flee) **and a guard** (Block halves, Dodge misses three in ten plus the class's and gear's dodge, Brace takes three quarters and gives mana, Counter takes it and hits back at half). Enemies have moves by weight; minis and bosses wind up a heavy one for a round that then hits two and a half times as hard, so the guard matters; they shrug off stuns. Twelve abilities, three ranks each, two per class from the start; classes carry their own crit and dodge. Xp, levels with growth, death to the nearest town **through open areas** with gear kept. A boss whose area beyond is not laid yet lays it the moment it falls, before the `opened` event.

### The client
The board draws each area's ground, covers closed areas, shows the bosses with level and countdown, badges spawns, hints on tap, lights only what is open, frames the open areas on Map; **a grown area is drawn the moment it is laid** (ground, name, roads, spots, boss label, cover) and the camera's bounds widen with the map; a three-line HUD with a chip row (dice cards, the gambler, an errand, a full bag's piece, a level's pick) and Map, World, Bag and Log buttons; **the atlas** (the areas by tier, bosses, kills, errands, where you are, Go to frame one, the settings behind it); **culling** of what the camera cannot see; **the first minutes** said once; the fight screen's two taps with a mana bar and status lines; the shop's Buy and Sell; the bag scene; the world ticks once a minute; the character screen says Zite.

### Balance (`tools/simulate.ts`, `docs/state/rules.md` → Balance)
Bots of each class play from Ashford under a plain policy, and each class is thrown at each boss level by level in the plain gear of the rank. **The first numbers were far too easy**: no deaths in three hundred turns, every class at the level cap, a level-one Warrior with no gear beating the Warden, and a stun-lock. After the retune: level 5 around turn 55; nobody beats the Warden under level 3; at level 5 in copper every class but the Rogue wins nine in ten; the Briar King and the Matriarch fall at their own level in the area's gear for everyone but the Rogue, who needs a level more. The simulation also found a real bug, now fixed and tested: a character beaten next to the Briar Gate woke in Frosthold, behind the boss, stranded. With the world growing, the bots were thrown at the first three grown bosses too, and the growth a tier set so that at the boss's own level in the rank's plain gear most classes win nine in ten. With the kits, the uniques and the readable enemies the wall was run once more with the level's whole kit: the first kits were far too strong, were reined in, and the bosses grew a tenth; a boss at its own level now falls for most classes nine times in ten, the Rogue and the Mage a little less, and two levels under it is half to eight in ten.

## What the tests cover (263 tests; `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` pass)
`board.test.ts` (the ring, the world **and two worlds grown ten areas** sound and drawable, every roll usable with every area open and with only the areas up to one's own open, the world's shape), `generate.test.ts` (the peek, the cells, an area's shape, names and creatures, growth by tier, growing the board as a copy, idempotent and the same whatever the order, twenty areas each reachable over its passage, the hints, the Matriarch's fall laying gen-1 in play and gen-1's boss laying gen-2), `kits.test.ts` (the four meters, every new ability, the level's pick), `enemies.test.ts` (the intent told and used, every effect, the bosses' phases), `uniques.test.ts` (every unique and every power in play, what bosses, minis and mobs drop, the version-6 save), `quests.test.ts` (the errands offered, taken, declined, moved along and paid; the trainer; the bag's limit and its question; the flasks), `vaults.test.ts` (every theme's event, the shapes and their vaults, a vault locked and opened with its key, the version-8 save), `world.test.ts` (the builder, passages, bounds, every error), `gear.test.ts` (ranks and the growth past the tables, rarity odds and boosts, rolled bounds, `stats` with every affix), `game.test.ts` (every landing and its cooldown, the surprises' odds, the gamble, spawns, closed areas, migrations from 1 to 5), `fight.test.ts` (a round pinned from one seed for each class's kit, the guards' arithmetic, wind-ups, every effect, stuns shrugged off, loot by role, a boss opening an area, death with gear kept and never behind a gate), `items.test.ts` (shop, sell, equip, unequip, drop, dice cards), `shared.test.ts` (joining, the delta, two bots and a client folding every delta), `coop.test.ts` (the world boss coming, fought together, paid by share, leaving; the notes left, replaced, capped, faded, read; the version-9 save), `purity.test.ts`, the server actor on the ring including its world tick and its deltas, and `hub.test.ts` (real sockets on a free port: two players joining and seeing each other, an intent answered and told to the others in one bundled event, the same id from the store, the account stamped whatever the client wrote, every refusal, a new socket with the token and a new token from the code, a flood cut off, leave, the tick reaching everyone).

## What is verified how
- **By tests**: everything in the rules above.
- **By the headless driver** (`tools/drive-board.mjs`, Chromium at 412 by 915 with touch, **86 checks pass**): the character screen; the camera; the covered areas and the three bosses on the board; hints on a wild spot, on the Iron Gate and on a covered spot; a framed roll, drag, pinch, wheel; a reload mid-choice; an old save at version 6; a wild spot opening the fight; the enemy's next move and the class meter on the fight screen; the abilities menu, Charge then Counter, Flee, Attack and Block to the end; a reload mid-fight; Continue; the shop's buys, Sell; the bag's Wear, Take off, Drop; the +1 and Exactly N chips; the gambler's chips; a merchant's shop; a potion as a move; a shrine; a level crossed on screen; a death and the walk back; a level-one Warrior beaten by the Warden; a spawned mini-boss cleared; a level's pick answered in the chips; the trainer teaching War Cry; an errand asked on landing in Ashford and taken; a full bag's piece sold from the chips; the World button's atlas, Go framing Thornwood, the settings' toggles kept; the mana potion among the moves; the Iron Gate's boss dropping a unique or an epic, and the Iron Gate and the Briar Gate opening their areas; **the Frost Matriarch laying and opening the first grown area, drawn spot for spot with the map wider, its gate's hint naming the next area by tier, a reload keeping it drawn, and its boss laying the second**; reset. No page errors.
- **By the two-phone driver** (`tools/drive-coop.mjs`, a server of its own, **19 checks pass**): the character screen says where the world is; A makes an account (the token and the code on the phone); B joins and both see each other (marks, "with …", "online · 2 here", a line about the newcomer); A rolls and walks and B sees the mark move; A reloads through the connect screen as the same character; the server is stopped (the HUD says reconnecting) and started again and both phones come back on their own; B rolls after that and A sees it; a third phone brings A's character with her code; the settings show the address and the code; then world bosses are planted in the database and the server restarted: both phones draw the badges, A leaves "Danger!" from the chips on her spot and B gets the mark, the line and the hint, A rolls onto a world boss (the screen says so) and strikes once, and B sees the shared HP drop in his state, on the badge and in the hint; no page errors.
- **By the bots**: the curve above, from the rules alone.
- **Only by reading**: how the two-tap round feels on a phone, the look of the grown areas beyond their screenshots, and the frame rate on a real phone with a few hundred spots drawn (the headless run is software GL at 60 fps).

## Checklist for the local session (browser pane at phone size, then Robin's phone)
1. **First open**: the character screen says Zite; pick a class; the meadows at follow zoom, Thornwood and Frostpeak dark under their covers, the Iron Gate's "Thornwood Warden · level 6" at the top right.
2. **Tap spots**: a wild spot says the levels and the creatures; the Iron Gate says what it opens; a spot in a covered area says which boss opens it; the Summit says "Beat it to open Emberfall (tier 4)".
3. **Map** frames the meadows; **Back** glides home. Drag and pinch as before.
4. **A roll into the wilds**: most landings fight. Read the orange line under the enemy: it says what comes next; Block a wind-up, Dodge a poison. The move row, then the guard row; watch your meter fill (dots under your HP) and spend it on Execute, Smoke Bomb, Time Warp or the Hawk once you have them. Die once: wake in the nearest town with less gold, gear kept.
5. **Level 4**: two ability names appear as chips after the fight; tap one. Shrines still teach the other later.
6. **The Iron Gate's loot**: the Warden drops a unique half the time (orange in the bag, with a line on what it does): wear it and feel the rule change.
7. **Chest, spring, shrine**: give once, then "Empty for now; again in m:ss"; the spring gives a potion and a mana potion; the shrine teaches a third ability.
8. **Ashford again**: it asks an errand (Take it); its shop has a Train tab, War Cry for 60 gold; fill the bag with twelve pieces and the thirteenth asks to be sold or left.
9. **Tinker Cart or a town**: Buy a copper piece, Sell it back at half, the Bag's Wear and Take off; the HUD's numbers follow.
10. **The Iron Gate**: too hard at level 1 to 3 (it should feel so); at level 5 with copper gear it should fall for most classes; Thornwood's cover lifts; the gate counts down five minutes and the Warden is back.
11. **The Summit** (or a planted strong save, as the driver does): the Matriarch falls, "Emberfall is open!", the map widens east and the new area appears with its own ground colour, names and a boss at its far end; Map frames all four; tap its gate for the hint about the fifth area.
12. **Spawns**: leave the page open; within a few minutes a "!" or "$" badge bobs over a wild spot; land there.
13. **World**: the atlas lists the areas; Go frames one; Settings: try fewer effects and large text.
14. **The frame log** from the phone with the whole meadows drawn and a fight played, and once with a grown area on the board, with culling on.
15. **The world on the server** (`docs/state/server.md`, "Running it for friends"): `npm run server`, `npm run tunnel`, open the client once on the phone as `…/?server=wss://<the tunnel address>`; the character screen says "the world at …"; Begin; the HUD says "online". A second phone (or a private window) with the same address: both stand on the board, "with …" in the place line, the other's mark moves when they roll. Kill the server: "reconnecting (n)…"; start it: "online" again without a tap. Settings → Account: the code; type it on the other phone's character screen ("I have a code from another phone"): the same character there.
16. **Together** (two phones online): tap the spot you stand on → the four note chips → one; the other phone taps that spot and reads the note. Wait for "A world boss rages in …" (about once in fifty minutes; or plant one as the driver does): land there on both phones, watch the purple badge's HP fall from either side, and when it falls both get a share.

Note for the merge: main gained the Art Director's assets and `docs/state/art.md` meanwhile; this branch merges main, with the state-docs index taking both sides' rows. The Art Director's meadow monsters (Puffwort, Honey Bumble, Bramble Bun) are not the rules' meadow mobs (Slime, Moor Wolf, Bandit, Marsh Wisp) yet; that is a naming to settle when the sprites go on the board.

title: Fixing Netlify deploy error by using local expo CLI with npx or pnpm exec
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/ubiquitous-frangipane-9268b4/agent-runs/6ae6b6936796840ae21812b1

🤖 **Agent:** Claude (claude-opus-5-5)

💬 **Prompt:** The Netlify deploy errored, with the following guidance provided:

The build fails at [line 87](#L87) because the `expo` CLI is not found in the system path.

**Cause:** The build command `expo export -p web` requires the `expo` CLI to be available, ...

✅ **Result:**

The Netlify deploy was failing because the site was set up to run `expo export -p web`, but this repository is not an Expo app — it is the Scramjet proxy demo (a Node/Fastify server plus a static front-end). Netlify had picked up Expo because of the `app.json` file, so the `expo` command didn't exist during the build.

A `netlify.toml` now sets the build command to `pnpm run build` and the publish directory to `dist`. It also sends the cross-origin isolation headers that the Node server used to add. Settings in this file take precedence over the old build settings in the Netlify UI. The new `build` script (`scripts/build-static.js`) copies the `public/` front-end and the Scramjet, libcurl transport and bare-mux client files into `dist/`, using the same `/scram/`, `/libcurl/` and `/baremux/` paths the server serves them from. I ran the script locally and it produced the expected `dist/` folder, but I haven't seen a Netlify deploy succeed yet.

There's an important limitation: proxying needs a Wisp WebSocket server, and Netlify cannot host one. The deployed page loads, but browsing through the proxy only works if you point it at a Wisp server hosted somewhere else. To do that, set the `WISP_URL` environment variable (for example `wss://your-wisp-host/wisp/`). The build writes it into `config.js`, and the front-end now uses it in place of its own host. Running `pnpm start` locally works as before.

title: Use Anura as the default Wisp relay

title: Past-only backfill stream stalls: 72% of visit slots revisit complete relays, never-run relays go hours unattempted and fail on permanent refusals
body:
## Summary

A temporary past-only stream (`backfillMutesReports`, kinds 1984 + 10000) stopped making progress after about 2 hours. Of its 1,534 relays, 577 have never completed a page, and `neverRun` fell by only **6 in 71 minutes** (586 at 19:09Z → 580 at 20:20Z), while all 8 visit slots stayed busy.

Visits themselves aren't slow: most end in under 10 s. Measured on staging, the slots go elsewhere:

1. **72% of visits went to relays that were already complete** for this stream, even though it re-fetches once a year.
2. **Most never-run relays weren't attempted at all.** In 2 h of log, 75 of the 364 named failing relays got a visit; the other 289 got none.
3. **Those that are attempted fail for reasons that won't change on retry**:
   - kind-restricted relays (`restricted: this relay only serves kinds …`, `blocked: kinds N not allowed`);
   - NIP-42-only relays;
   - dead hosts (most of them `.onion` or `ws://`);
   - and refusals we cause ourselves: **150 `rate-limited` / `too many subscriptions` refusals across all streams in 2 h**, 106 of them reading *"there is a bug in the client, no one should be making so many requests"*.

The same thing happened to the previous temporary stream (`backfillFollowLists`, kind 3, 2026-10-28/29): `neverRun` stopped near 474 and never moved, for the same reasons.

The full list of failing relays is at the end.

## Build

```
vespa-relay   sync + relay sha-022dc78 (quartz 2.4.0)
store         493fe01d9ea7
namespace     vespa-eventstore-staging (brainstormk2), sync pod started 2026-10-29 13:55Z
```

Stream config (same shape as `backfillReposts`, which runs beside it with `visitConcurrency = 16`):

```hocon
backfillMutesReports {
    visitConcurrency = 8
    maxLiveConcurrency = 1
    refetchConcurrency = 1
    negentropyConcurrency = 1
    dir = "down"
    filter = { "kinds": [1984, 10000], "until": 1793289600 }   # 2026-10-29 16:00:00Z
    relaySource = [ { filter = { "kinds": [30166], "#l": ["prime"], "authors": ["4aab697d…b483"] }
                      maxAgeSeconds = 172800, refreshSeconds = 120 } ]
    exclude = [ "wss://purplepag.es", "wss://profiles.nostr1.com", "wss://indexer.coracle.social",
                "wss://user.kindpag.es", "wss://directory.yabu.me" ]
    refetchThePastSeconds = 31536000
}
```

## What we measured

**Sources.** The sync state file, copied at 20:28Z and checked with md5. The pod log from 18:33:52Z to 20:35:13Z; `kubectl logs` doesn't return anything older for this pod. `/stats.json`, sampled every 12 s for 313 s from about 20:29Z.

### 1. Coverage state

`sync-cursors.json`, key `backfillMutesReports` / `{"kinds":[1984,10000],"until":1793289600}`:

| | relays |
|---|---|
| roster (`/stats.json`) | 1,534 |
| `complete: true` | 944 |
| `complete: false` (partial) | 13 |
| no record at all | ~577 |

`schedule`: `{"job":"re-fetching","everySec":31536000,"due":0,"neverRun":580,"waiting":954}`. `limits[visiting]`: `streamCap 8, inUse 8, deferred 4,751,578`.

### 2. The slots mostly revisit relays that are already complete

The 313 s sample saw **50 distinct relays** pass through the 8 slots. Most were held 0–10 s; one, relay.dreamith.to, streamed 20k events over 800 s. Checked against the state file:

| coverage of the visited relay | visits |
|---|---|
| complete | **36** |
| no record | 12 |
| partial | 2 |

The same thing shows in the aborts. Of 191 aborted `backfillMutesReports` visits in the log window, **66 were on relays already marked complete**. Their asks:

- 27 asked `since` = within a day before `until`;
- 23 asked `since` more than a day before `until`;
- 16 asked from the floor, `since 1577836800`.

Revisits don't seem to update the record: `fullAt` is more than 3 h old on 854 of the 944 complete relays, and under 1 h on only 4.

For **all 944** complete relays, `max` (the newest event seen) is below `until`, and the gap can be as small as 103 s. That's a relay whose newest matching event is older than `until`.

**Hypothesis, not confirmed:** the window `(max, until]` is treated as uncovered, so a complete relay is visited again for an empty tail it can never fill. The log has no line for a successful visit, so the log alone can't tell whether these revisits count as done.

### 3. Never-run relays are rarely attempted, and fail when they are

Of the 364 failing relays we could name (log or `/stats.json` rows):
- **75** got at least one aborted visit in the 2 h window.
- **289** got none. `/stats.json` lists them as `notStarted`.
- For relays attempted more than once, the median gap between attempts was **37 min** (p10 16 min, p90 62 min).

`/stats.json` `relays.rows` is capped at 1,000 rows (5,152 omitted), so about 226 of the ~577 no-record relays can't be named from it or from 2 h of log.

Abort reasons on those 75 relays (125 aborts):

| reason (sync) | aborts |
|---|---|
| the relay closed the subscription | 47 |
| the dial never landed | 36 |
| the relay went quiet inside the page | 28 |
| the relay would not accept our NIP-42 identity | 14 |

What the relays said, deduplicated. Most of these won't change on a retry:

- **Kind-restricted:**
  - `restricted: this relay only serves kinds …` (×3)
  - `blocked: kinds N not allowed`
  - `error: bad req: filter validation failed: kind not allowed`
  - `blocked: this index relay does not serve those event kinds`
  - `invalid-filter: only wallet kinds are allowed`
  - `blocked: invalid query, must have 'h', 'e' or 'a' tag` (×4)
  - `restricted: request one chat group and supported chat kinds explicitly`
- **Auth / membership:** `auth-required: …` (×9 across variants), `restricted: members only`.
- **Relay-side bug:** `error: scraper, …/pocket-db/src/lib.rs:782:48` (chorus / pocket, ×5 relays).
- **Size:** `error: an event was too large to deliver`, `message too large`.
- **Dead or unreachable:** 94 of the 364 are `.onion`, and 97 are plain `ws://`.

### 4. Refusals we cause ourselves (all streams, same 2 h)

150 aborts carry a rate-limit or subscription-cap message:

```
103  rate-limited: there is a bug in the client, no one should be making so many requests
 12  rate-limited: too many messages
  6  rate-limited: too many messages — the socket carried N event(s) on N subscription(s) …
  4  rate-limited: too many subscriptions
  4  rate-limited: too many messages (limit 12/min); slow down
  4  blocked: already 50 subscriptions from this IP
  3  rate-limited: there is a bug in the client, … (socket variant)
  3  rate-limited: estimated query cost N exceeds N
```

These come mostly from `wot.*` relays: wot.dergigi.com, wot.nostr.net, wot.nostr.party, wot.czas.plus, wot.sudocarlos.com, wot.rejecttheframe.xyz, wot.mwaters.net, wot.makenomistakes.ca, plus nostrelites.org and basspistol.org. Each is visited by several streams, and the temporary streams add more visits on top. Across the 2 h, aborted visits per stream: contentViaOutbox 359, profileViaOutbox 296, backfillReposts 211, backfillMutesReports 191, assertions 14, indexers 7.

### 5. One slot lingers in the tail

`wss://nproxy.kristapsk.lv/` held a slot for 508 s and counting, with 3 events, showing `doing: "draining queued heals, then the tail"`, and `pagingUntil` 1793289459, 141 s before `until`. With `maxLiveConcurrency = 1` and an `until` in the past, it isn't clear what that tail waits for.

## Questions

1. Why does a past-only stream keep revisiting relays already marked `complete`? Is `(max, until]` the window it re-asks?
2. How does the rotation order relays? 289 never-run relays went 2 h without an attempt while complete relays were being revisited.
3. Could a permanent refusal (a kind restriction, `auth-required` with no NIP-42 identity it accepts, `invalid-filter`) close the band as unreadable, rather than leave it to be retried forever and keep `neverRun` from reaching 0?
4. Could `rate-limited` / `too many subscriptions` back off per host across streams, rather than per (stream, relay)?
5. Could a successful visit log a line, so completion can be read from the log as aborts can?

title: Vexel 1.2: every repo game plays in Vexel, Caver works out of the box
body:
Builds on #2 (includes its commits).

## What changes
- **Caver** uses nexSite's Scramjet 2 + libcurl + Wisp setup with the public `wss://wisp.mercurywork.shop/` server, so it works with no setup. Settings → *Caver server* lets a visitor switch servers if a school blocks that one.
- **Game mirror** (`public/mirror-sw.js`): the service worker streams games from techmaster2013's public repos under `gh/<repo>/…`, strips popunder ads and trackers, fixes root-relative paths, and (`?own`) ignores dead jsDelivr/githack `<base>` links. This is how game-hub (14 GB) and the T9 library play without copying them into Pages. jsDelivr now blocks most of the genizy CDN copies those ports used.
- **Player**: every game plays inside Vexel (no new tabs). Records carry an ordered `sources` list; **⇄ Source** switches to the next copy, and frame-refusing sites open through Caver inside the player.
- Pages workflow reads the `game-pack-v2` release (catalog from techmaster2013/vex-games `vexel-1.2-catalog`).

## Before merging
1. Merge vex-games `vexel-1.2-catalog`.
2. Publish the pack: `gh release create game-pack-v2 game-pack.tar.gz --repo techmaster2013/vexel --title "Game pack for Vexel 1.2"` (tarball of vex-games without `.git`).

## Tested
- `pnpm test`: 23 pass (4 new mirror tests).
- Headless Chromium on a local Pages build under `/vexel/`: Karlson and Granny (game-hub/granny mirrors), Eaglercraft (local), Retro Bowl (gn-math frame), the Google baseball doodle (Caver in the player), Caver browsing example.com over the public Wisp server.
- Smoke test of all mirror-first games (loads, missing files, exceptions); remaining issues are upstream (e.g. 3 corrupted OMORI plugin files in game-hub).

title: Fix transport safety, cookie isolation, and browser compatibility
body:
Fixes #478, #476, #460, #461, #482, #453, #465, #471, #466, #467, #484, #485 and #486. Addresses #483 and parts of #454, #456, #462, #470 and #487.

## Changes

- Honor split HTML BOMs over conflicting charset headers and rewrite CSS image-set string URLs.
- Correct WebSocket send/close states and Web IDL conversions, contain bridge send failures, and account for queued UTF-8/binary bytes. Discarded CLOSING/CLOSED sends also add bytes, verified against direct Chromium. Bridge acceptance is not network drain.
- Separate SharedWorker identities by type/credential mode and close heartbeat MessageChannel ports after the final rewrite stream settles.
- Use collision-free cookie origin keys with migration; serialize profile snapshots, merge restored root assignments safely, and fail closed on invalid/unreadable/unsupported snapshots.
- Revalidate cache responses through normal transport policy and client/credential context. Session-authenticated views stay out of the shared page cache.
- Protect assignment/update/delete targets using AST spans. Add per-site legacy/hybrid/off location controls with bounded AST work, owner-page policy for inline/CDN/cached scripts, and bounded skip/rewrite diagnostics.
- Correct GIS origin/ss_domain parameters only for this deployment and verified virtual page context. Provider authentication acceptance is not guaranteed.
- Bound relay queues and preserve per-request credit negotiation. Clean up malformed chunks/headers, failed dispatch/credit/cancel ports, bodyless responses and pending pulls.
- Represent delivery certainty explicitly. Private provenance drives replay decisions; stale pre-dispatch claims become unknown after adapter invocation. Typed errors retain causes without hiding stall/reset health signals. Aborts and one-shot bodies never replay; unknown non-idempotent writes remain terminal.
- Emit fixed, trace-correlated delivery diagnostics without copying error causes or bodies; regression tests check client separation.
- Centralize conservative live/cache response planning, separate behavior policy from wire routing, and expose adaptive-picker evidence through opt-in bounded tracing.
- Classify ordinary asset-recovery exclusions as informational skips and remove a false-positive ciphertext substring assertion from session tests.
- Keep userinfo-carrying URL literals (Sentry DSN shape, scheme://key@host) verbatim in JS string-literal passes; HTML attributes and script srcs keep routing, and the gate inspects the authority only (#499, tests included).
- Virtualize the Twitch embed `parent=` parameter to the embedding page's hostname at the fetch seam (`virtualTwitchParent`, the #112 co= class: engine-valued parent params on `player.twitch.tv` and `embed.twitch.tv` `/embed/` paths are rewritten to the referrer-derived page hostname, real-domain embeds pass through untouched; 9 tests mirroring the ogs suite) (#506).
- Emit one TRANSPORT diag row when the Ghostery matcher parses empty or partial from a 200 junk list body, and never install it: a sanity floor on the parsed network-filter count, a kept previously loaded good matcher across a bad refresh, and the retry cooldown (4 tests) (#500).
- Resolve manifest `__MSG_*__` name/description placeholders from the package's `_locales/<default_locale>/messages.json` at install and reload (unresolved placeholders keep their literal bytes and warn), and give `zl:listExt`/`zl:extInfo` a token-gated `iconPath` for the largest manifest icon, served on one non-navigation fetch per minted token (6 tests; the options-page white screen is still open) (#504). Implement MV2 `background.page` support by extracting the page's classic inline and external scripts in document order and running them in the background sandbox, with `background.page` taking precedence over `background.scripts` exactly as in Chrome; move the compatibility matrix entry from `no` to `partial` because no DOM exists for the page (a DOM-touching script fails the boot with the recorded error) and the page itself is not browsable; a missing page or script file fails the boot honestly (7 tests) (#505). Keep the streaming CSS image-set boundary check chunk-independent by carrying the byte preceding the retained tail, so a chunk split before `image-set(` no longer turns an identifier tail into a rewrite candidate; regression test asserts the issue repro across every split (tree-wide rustfmt hygiene on two pre-existing #499 hunks included) (#507).

## Validation

Current combined tree passes locally: **1,712 app tests across 165 files**, typecheck, production build, diff checks, and both real Chromium fixtures (location-policy WASM execution and WebSocket discarded-send accounting). Bootstrap is **39,419 bytes**, below the unchanged 39,424-byte gate. The unchanged Rust tree previously passed **187 rewriter tests**, formatting and Clippy with warnings denied.

Both browser fixtures are wired into browser CI. The local WASM fixture used an unoptimized release artifact after the external Binaryen download failed; CI optimization settings are unchanged. [Latest GitHub Actions run](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40329642048) is still running at this update. Browser/compat jobs are skipped for PR triggers, so a green PR workflow does not establish full proxied compatibility.

## Remaining gates

- #454: all three acceptance fault phases (before connect, after headers, after acceptance) are covered by `suite/e2e/delivery-fault.mjs` (pinned contract, strict POST===1 per phase, honest-502 checks). The reachable seam is fixed: non-idempotent requests ride a per-request fresh HTTPSession (commit edce0a1), engine gates verified correct by probe runs. Remaining violation is below every Zeolite seam: the vendored libcurl wasm build deterministically re-dispatches a request whose connection dies in the complete-upload/awaiting-response state (5/5 harness runs), which vanilla curl would not do (its retry requires a reused connection). Fix requires the vendored libcurl-wasm seam, same class as #496. No exactly-once delivery claim beyond the pinned harness.
- #456: default-off migration, total candidate buffering, full proxied site/scoreboard rollout and worker/eval stages. Generic 404s never auto-enable rewriting.
- #462/#470: network-level drain signals and cooperative throttling for legacy relay peers remain unavailable.
- #487: content-aware AST proof, bounded compatibility learning and safe per-site adaptation remain open.
- #481: Claude black screen still needs reliable reproduction and a verified cause.
- #477/#452/#455/#451: secure guest execution, CSP translation, browser identity measurements and complete CAPTCHA-stage tracing remain open. Same-global untrusted guest execution is not implemented or claimed safe.

**Keep this PR open and unmerged.**

### #477 guest registration groundwork and #452 CSP preparation

- **#477 (P0/P1 preparation, not guest execution):** added `app/src/kernel/guests/registration.ts`, a bounded pure registry keyed by the full canonical virtual origin and scope, with strict cross-origin, script/scope, stored-record and ambiguous-path checks; correct longest-scope matching and explicit teardown. Added adversarial tests. Kept the existing page-side `swshim.ts` unchanged after inspecting the strict bootstrap size budget—there is no new runtime guest execution or implied service-worker controller.
- **#452 (off by default):** added `app/src/csp-translation.ts`, a pure strict policy planner that emits candidates only for narrowly specified deny-only `object-src`, `base-uri` and `form-action` with `'none'`. Policies with URL sources, `'self'`, nonce/hash, strict-dynamic, sandbox, report-only, duplicates or other unhandled semantics return typed unsupported results. Real response CSP stripping is unchanged; neither headers nor HTML meta tags are rewritten/enforced.
- Added dedicated tests in `guest-registration.test.ts` and `csp-translation.test.ts`; documented prerequisites, security limits and the rollout block in `docs/virtual-service-worker-phase2.md` and `docs/limitations.md`.

These are safe groundwork slices, **not full fixes** for #477 or #452. Isolated worker execution needs a killable separate realm and a security review. CSP adoption needs engine-route-aware source matching, injection fidelity and actual Chromium allow/block fixtures. No safety parity or completion claim. **Do not merge.**

**#477/#452 groundwork validation (2fc8957f8340):** [GitHub Actions run 40333162441](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40333162441) completed successfully: Rust, WASM and app checks (including the new guest-registration and CSP planner unit tests) passed. Browser and compatibility suites are skipped on PRs. Neither feature is enabled as a new security boundary; both issues remain open.

### Reproduced small bug fixes (#488, #489, #493)

- **#493:** Page/worker shared `wsPayload` rejects typed arrays/DataViews backed by `SharedArrayBuffer` before the WebSocket shim enqueues or counts their bytes, matching the reproduced Chromium `TypeError` conversion behavior. Ordinary ArrayBuffer views/offsets, blobs and text stay supported.
- **#489:** The anchor decoder now has a one-shot channel settle/cleanup path for normal, malformed, timeout, and synchronous send failure. It clears in-flight routes and releases both locally held ports; the worker also closes the one-shot decode reply port after responding.
- **#488:** The bounded document scan now advances independently of its 512-entry memo; a split relative/absolute pair is revisited at the window boundary, and a completed document does not endlessly rescan the evicted prefix. Attribute mutations reset the scan and an explicit late read can re-decode an evicted route. Verified by new 600-absolute-route, 300-pair, mutation and evicted-read regression fixtures.
- Dedicated Vitest coverage: `ws-shared-payload.test.ts`, `anchor-channel-lifetime.test.ts`, and `anchor-scan-progress.test.ts`.
- **Budget gate retained unchanged:** 39,424 minified bootstrap bytes; source has been compacted rather than raising the limit. Earlier CI revisions passed new tests but exceeded the size cap; the newest revision's size/build check must be verified before claiming this work CI green.

These are reproduced engine bugs, not an explanation for the reported Startpage favicon error (#492). Keep PR open and unmerged.

### #495 read-only Zeolite Doctor (implementation)

- Added `app/src/doctor.ts`: deterministic, bounded **passive** Doctor checks with explicit `pass/warn/fail/skipped/unknown` statuses. The response distinguishes `ok` (the API answered) from tri-state `healthy` (true, false, null for unverified/partial). It does not guess handshake, site identity, missing browser headers or unobserved WASM success.
- Added host-only `zl:doctor` control-plane command **before the normal bootstrap readiness gate**, so failed or stalled initialization produces an honest result. No `zl:doctor` entry in `PAGE_MESSAGES`; no cookie/transport/policy writes or debug-global log fallback. Existing message-lifecycle path does not flush cookie state for a Doctor read.
- Read-only evidence: boot result/deadline, observed transport lifecycle/selected engine/relay registration, primary WISP scheme (redacted; no URL exposure), host-supplied expected scope/version, engine degraded state, and passive KDL `policy.kdl`/`rules.kdl`/`siteconfig.kdl` load outcomes (loaded/missing/malformed/unavailable/never loaded). Loader changes do **not** initiate new fetches.
- Optional `probeAssets: true`: four fixed, same-origin, credential-free, no-redirect HEAD requests to SW-sibling bootstrap, codec, worker prelude and rewriter WASM. 1.5-second per-asset deadlines, coalescing of concurrent calls, strict status/MIME evaluation. 404 and HTML SPA fallback are failures; unsupported HEAD/timeouts are explicitly unverified. **No arbitrary target, upstream WISP authentication or TLS probes.**
- Optional `format: "kdl"`: bounded versioned, parseable `zeolite-doctor version=1` document with fixed diagnostic labels; no raw credentials, origin URLs, body data or secret exception messages. This can later join #494's wider KDL log schema. **Zeolite ships no MCP server.**
- Tests: `doctor.test.ts`, `doctor-loader.test.ts`, and host-gate/boot-failure regressions in `control.test.ts`. Documentation in `docs/doctor.md` and `docs/integration-guide.md`.
- Remaining acceptance: no final-head CI workflow currently reported by GitHub for these commits, and no Chromium browser integration run. Do not claim full #495 completion or merge PR until tests/build (including the unchanged strict bootstrap budget) have passed.

The prior unmerged PR work and all previously noted limitations remain in place.


### #495 standalone Doctor UI follow-through

- `app/devtools.html` now contains a dedicated **Zeolite Doctor** panel with manual **Inspect**, **Check bundle assets**, and **Export KDL** buttons.
- `app/src/devtools.ts` calls the host-only `zl:doctor` API through a one-shot MessageChannel (explicit close/timeout/error handling), renders only bounded fixed check labels via `textContent`, and downloads `zeolite-doctor.kdl` locally through a temporary Blob URL. No automatic network probe or MCP server is introduced.
- `docs/doctor.md` documents standalone UI and how it differs from host-owned (e.g. LobsterBrowse) DevTools/MCP integration.
- **Validation caveat:** No final-HEAD Actions run is associated with these commits in the GitHub connector yet. Actual browser UI behavior and size/build gates must still be verified; do not mark the feature security- or browser-validated until then.


### #494 request-scoped KDL debugger groundwork

- Added `app/src/compat-debugger.ts`: a pure, bounded request timeline from existing DIAG, network and opt-in tracing rings. Only allowlisted lifecycle/transport/rewrite enums and bounded numeric facts are exported. Arbitrary page-controlled messages, destinations, headers, cookies, credentials, error text, policy rule strings and trace original/result contents are **never serialized**, even if a preexisting ring contains unsanitized strings.
- Added **host-only `zl:exportDiagnostics`**: requires a caller-authenticated host page, an engine-generated trace ID, its SW-owned `traceClient` mapping, and a **currently live same-origin proxied client**. Missing/mismatched/stale/failed lookup returns `identity-unavailable`; never expose the global ring. The preflight does not wait on a potentially wedged boot promise and skips cookie persistence.
- Output is `scope: "request"`, `collection: "observed" | "no-evidence"` plus a versioned, parser-friendly KDL text. Absence of an event is **not** proof of success. The existing bounded rings remain in memory, no extra request instrumentation or transport mutation is enabled.
- Standalone `app/devtools.html` / `app/src/devtools.ts`: select a network row with both worker-attributed `clientId` and `traceId` to enable **Export selected request KDL**. Worker revalidates ownership; UI downloads a local `zeolite-request.kdl`, handles timeout/stale identity, and does not add an MCP server.
- Unit/negative tests: `compat-debugger.test.ts`, expanded `control.test.ts` for host isolation, stale client, rejected client enumeration, adversarial unsanitized canaries, ordering and KDL parsing.
- Documented in `docs/compatibility-debugger.md`.
- **Not full #494 completion**: document-generation isolation across navigations, frame-wide timeline, source-rule/multi-transport proof, common Doctor+debugger export envelope and real Chromium end-to-end validation remain. Do not claim a completed per-document debugger.

### #496 authenticated WISP — implementation deferred after protocol audit

- WISP v2.1 defines `INFO` extension metadata for password (0x02) and key (0x03) auth; Zeolite's server verifies these extensions after receiving the client's payloads.
- However the shipped browser transport uses **vendored `@mercuryworkshop/libcurl-transport` and epoxy**, configured with WISP endpoints; the separate `crates/wisp-wasm` helper is not proven to own those vendor handshakes and currently emits **empty client extensions**.
- Do **not** inject secrets into WebSocket URLs/subprotocols or claim the standalone helper patch would enable real browser auth. No password/key provisioner or handshake has been merged or fabricated.
- #496 stays open until the precise vendor client authentication seam and real authenticated browser/server test can be verified.

### Validation

No Actions workflow run is currently returned for the latest PR head by GitHub; source-level changes and new tests are committed, **not yet reported passing CI or Chromium compatibility**. Keep PR #480 open/unmerged.


### Four experimental selectors (Beta secret picker integration)

- Registered exactly `experimental.adaptiveTransit`, `experimental.hybridLocation`, `experimental.cspTranslation`, and `experimental.virtualSW` on the **existing host-only** `zl:config` path. All choices are false by default and stored per worker lifetime; malformed/unknown keys fail atomically.
- `zl:config` acknowledgment and `zl:ping` report **requested vs effective** values. These flags are **selection-only** at this stage: the effective state is false for all four until independent compatibility/security acceptance. Existing conservative transit planning and per-site location KDL configuration are untouched. CSP enforcement and guest worker execution are **not** enabled.
- Added `app/src/experimental-flags.ts`, `experimental-flags.test.ts`, control-plane gate/ack tests, and `docs/experimental-flags.md`.
- LobsterBrowse **Beta** branch `beta/zeolite-nativetransit` has been updated separately: its existing five-click Home-wordmark Debug picker offers the four choices, persists them in the existing override store, and pushes them to app/content workers. Beta CI has a new local preference-schema test. **No new experimental runtime was implemented**.
- Pending: complete CI/typecheck/build/browser validation; Beta's currently deployed older worker may ignore these new choices until an updated engine bundle is shipped. Zeolite PR #480 remains **open and unmerged**.


### Experimental runtime follow-through (bounded feature gates)

- **CSP (#452):** `experimental.cspTranslation` now wires to the live served HTML-document path. It restores ONLY a `planCspTranslation` candidate of deny-only `object-src`, `base-uri` or `form-action 'none'` to the downstream response. Every other upstream CSP remains stripped; report-only policy stays removed. A CSP-enabled document skips CSP-less page-cache hits so it uses live upstream security headers. OFF by default. Added direct allow/deny boundary tests. **Full CSP translation, enforcement comparisons in Chromium, and bootstrap compatibility remain open.**
- **Adaptive NativeTransit (#487):** `experimental.adaptiveTransit` gates additional *shadow-only* evidence on live and cached response paths; it never changes conservative `planResponseTransit`/body rewriting. OFF by default; `experimental.status` says `shadow-only`, and `effective` remains false (no new adaptive routing).
- **WISP password auth (#496):** canonical WISP v2 client INFO/password extension frame encoder `handshakeInfoPassword` in the existing `wisp-wasm` crate with Rust packet-roundtrip and input-bound tests. The vendored libcurl/Epoxy clients do **not** call this helper and no runtime credential path is connected. This is wire-code groundwork, NOT authenticated browser browsing. See `docs/wisp-auth-client.md`. No keys, URL credentials or speculative WebSocket monkeypatch added.
- **Virtual SW (#477), hybrid location (#456):** no new guest-script execution, unsafe sandbox, or automatic location rewrite has been activated. Existing registration and KDL behavior remains unchanged, the requested experimental flags stay `not-implemented`/`not-wired` and `effective:false`. Full guest execution requires an independently verified isolated origin/worker realm, scoped bridge, lifecycle and e2e browser tests, so I did not falsely claim it works.
- **LobsterBrowse Beta:** existing five-click hidden Debug picker remains the flag selector and now distinguishes the narrow CSP subset from shadow-only/unavailable flags in its acknowledgment text.
- Tests expanded for experimental enable/deny, CSP enforcement, and canonical password packet. **GitHub connector returns no Actions workflows for latest HEAD, so builds, typechecks, Rust tests and Chromium behavior have not been verified at this revision.** PR #480 remains open and must not merge on this evidence alone.


### CI gate repairs and direct verification (2026-10-26)

- Read GitHub Actions **run [40364050197](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40364050197)** directly. Earlier connector workflow lookup returned no runs, but the GitHub Actions API confirms this run failed in **two concrete places**: `cargo fmt --all --check` for the new WISP password encoder, and **one** `doctor.test.ts` KDL control-character fixture. The earlier app suite recorded **1777 passed / 1 failed**.
- Applied the exact rustfmt diff to `crates/wisp-wasm/src/lib.rs` without changing its behavior; corrected the Doctor fixture to use a real `\u0000` test escape instead of a literal escaped backslash-u sequence.
- Another fresh run [40365452428](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40365452428) passed WASM, Rust and the app unit tests/typecheck/build but exposed a **real strict bootstrap budget regression**: `bootstrap.js` **39445 bytes**, at/over the hard 39424 byte gate.
- Compacted only repeated cross-origin scope `TypeError` wording in `app/src/swshim.ts`. Scope validation and its regression tests are preserved; **the limit was not increased**.
- At latest HEAD `464c6c33fd45d5780025294e910835eb55a05a19`, GitHub Actions [run 40366107606](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40366107606) now reports the **app job successful**, with `bootstrap.js: 39407 bytes` (17 bytes below the limit), and WASM successful. Rust/browser/compat work must still finish before calling full CI green.
- **Not fully implemented:** authenticated WISP in the vendored browser clients, isolated virtual SW guest script execution, real adaptive rewrite switching, full cross-origin hybrid location rewriting, and complete browser-verified CSP translation. Never mark those done or merge on source-only tests.


### Latest full CI verification (run 40366107606)

Verified directly via the GitHub Actions API for HEAD `464c6c33fd45d5780025294e910835eb55a05a19`: [run 40366107606](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40366107606) completed successfully. **All five jobs passed: Rust, WASM, app, browser and compatibility.** The app bootstrap is **39,407 bytes / 39,424 allowed** and the bootstrap size budget was not raised. The browser job passed WebSocket buffered bytes, location-policy fixture, main E2E, torture, reload-count and injector-differential suites.

This clears all CI regressions introduced in this PR revision. **It does not establish feature completion** for #496 (live authenticated vendor client), #477 (guest execution sandbox), #487 (adaptive rewriting beyond shadow mode), #456 (hybrid runtime), or full #452 (arbitrary CSP/Chromium enforcement). Those remain open with honest capability flags. Do not merge without explicit user direction.


### 2026-10-26 follow-up: safe runtime diagnostics, bootstrap gate

- **Confirmed regressions found and corrected in CI:** after earlier full-green [run 40366107606](https://github.com/lobsterbs/Zeolite/actions/runs/40366107606), the initial attempt to implement native multi-scope virtual registration in `swshim.ts` increased the strict compiled bootstrap from **39407 to 40190 bytes** (limit 39424). That experimental patch and tests were **reverted entirely** to the preceding CI-green implementation; this feature is NOT marked done. Guest execution remains blocked by the independent isolation/lifecycle/security requirements in #477.
- **#495 Doctor WISP URL diagnosis:** report a *confirmed configuration failure* for WebSocket URL userinfo credentials, fragments, invalid schemes; warn on query-bearing WSS URLs without echoing any query, credential or userinfo.
