title: Concern C-F (3.5) — Nourish read (Step 2)
body:
## Summary

- **Concern ID:** C-F (3.5) Nourish **read**. Explore + read-only recipe-detail `NourishCard`. This PR stays **draft**.
- **Compute:** deferred. `POST /api/nourish` is build-doc item 15, not this PR. A pantry miss does not trigger compute.
- **Findings that changed the plan (landed in §2 / §7.1 / §8 and `RelayDefaults.members`):**
  - Android’s My Kitchen › Nourish tab is an entry card (🥦 / **Explore Nourish**). The pantry read is Nourish Explore; recipe-detail `NourishCard` is a third surface.
  - Pantry serves unauthenticated 30078s when `authors` is pinned to the Nourish service pubkey and `kinds` is exclusively `[30078]`. `#d` / `#l` / `limit` only narrow (`isPublicNourishFilter`).
  - **Issue #6 no longer blocks Nourish read.** Use `RelayPool.query` / `queryReportingAuth`, not `GroupRelayPool`.
- Pinned filter is `NourishFilter.publicCorpus`. Unexpected AUTH on that REQ is an explicit error, never an empty Explore/card. A recipe with no Nourish data is a quiet miss. Kill switch `FeatureFlags.nourishEnabled` defaults **true**.
- Client publishes no Nourish events.
- `FINDINGS.md` and `GATE.md` are stripped from the tree; full text is below.

## Test plan

- [x] Filter-shape pin (`authors`/`kinds`; encoded keys `kinds`/`authors`/`limit`)
- [x] Parser goldens (Android `NourishParserTest` / v3+v4 macros)
- [x] Explore states (loading / empty / AUTH error / no-EOSE / sort / chips / degraded)
- [x] Quiet miss vs AUTH on recipe detail
- [x] Kill switch default on; off hides tab and card
- [x] Live canary (opt-in, no key): pinned REQ against pantry, EOSE, no AUTH (2.90s)
- [x] Gate: hermetic failure set identical to `origin/main`; no failures in new or touched files

---

# GATE — concern-3.5/nourish @ d499e65
Runner: xcodebuild test, iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.5, Xcode 26.6, -parallel-testing-enabled NO
Hermetic (-only-testing:wispTests): 633 passed / 4 failed / 9 skipped, 0 fatal errors.
  Failure set IDENTICAL to origin/main (98c29c9) on this box:
    FeedRenderableTests/mentionTaggedNoteFollowsReplyGate (#4)
    SafetyTests/notificationDropsReplyInBlockedSubThread
    SafetyTests/notificationIngestZapJudgedByResolvedActor
    SafetyTests/purgeNonWotQualifiedScrubsInMemoryItems (2 issues)
  No failures in new or touched files.
Live canary (NourishLiveTests, sentinel .nourish_live_enable, no key):
  pantryPinnedReq_eoseWithoutAuth -> EOSE received, no AUTH challenge, 2.90s
  (also confirms pantry still serves the pinned public filter unauthenticated)
Read path only; POST /api/nourish compute deferred to build-doc item 15.
pbxproj: no diff.

---

# FINDINGS — Concern C-F (3.5): Nourish

Branch `concern-3.5/nourish` at `2be233f` (`#49` is in the log:
`fix(3.1b): hidden-coordinate unsave consults resolved list, not memory;
harden save-toggle tests (#49)`). Remote is
`https://github.com/zapcooking/zapcooking_ios.git`.

Sources: Android at `/Users/sethsager/Projects/zap_cooking_android`
(behavioral contract), member-relay at `/Users/sethsager/Projects/member-relay`
(`relay/main.go`), frontend at `/Users/sethsager/Projects/zapcooking`,
iOS worktree, `ZAPCOOKING_IOS_BUILD.md` §2 / §7 / §8.

**No stop condition hit.** Android's pantry read is the pinned public
shape (authors + kinds `[30078]`); extra `#d` / `#l` / `limit` are
narrowing and allowed. Compute is `POST /api/nourish` on the frontend.
The client publishes no Nourish events. `GroupRelayPool` is not needed.

---

## Scope fork (read this first)

Android has **three** Nourish surfaces. This prompt says "My Kitchen tab
slot"; the build doc §8 3.5 describes the recipe-detail card; 3.2's iOS
placeholder already names Explore as C-F's job. They are not the same
feature.

| Surface | What it does | Compute? | Key? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **My Kitchen › Nourish tab** | Entry card only. Navigation. No REQ. | No | No (`CookbookSubTab.NOURISH(false)`) |
| **Nourish Explore** (pushed route) | Pantry 30078 corpus + 30023 resolve, ranked/filtered grid | No | No |
| **Recipe detail** | One 30078 by `#d`; miss → offer `POST /api/nourish` | Yes | Read: no. Compute: signing key |

iOS 3.2 already ported the kitchen entry card, button disabled, with an
explicit hand-off: "Concern C-F wires the Nourish explore route"
(`wisp/NourishPlaceholderView.swift:3–6`).

**Recommendation for Step 2 — ship read first:**

1. Enable the kitchen CTA → Explore (Android kitchen-tab contract).
2. Port pantry read + parser + Explore UI (what the CTA opens).
3. Port recipe-detail `NourishCard` as a **read-only** miss-is-quiet
   section (build-doc 3.5; otherwise tapping an Explore tile loses the
   profile).
4. **Defer compute** (`POST /api/nourish`, members-only, Computing /
   NotScored) to the follow-up the build doc already calls "15. Nourish
   compute + Nourish Explore" — Explore itself is read-only; compute
   lives on recipe detail. Frontend endpoint exists; this is a split of
   *surface*, not a missing API.

If Step 2 is forced to include compute in the same PR it is feasible
(finding 3), but it is a second Android concern (2.4b) on a second
screen. Ship read first.

---

## 1. Android's Nourish data model

**Kind / author.** Kind **30078** (NIP-78 app data), authored by a
fixed service pubkey — not the viewing user, not the recipe author:

```
fdd263f69f9e95a2a0a58ec3e7e8053011214fa66007d93b26d2f4717d31917b
```

Android `NourishParser.SERVICE_PUBKEY` / `KIND`
(`NourishParser.kt:84–87`); frontend `NOURISH_SERVICE_PUBKEY`
(`src/lib/nourish/types.ts:12`); member-relay `nourishServicePubkey`
(`relay/main.go:668–677`). All three match.

**Keyed to the recipe, not the user.** `#d` is
`nourish:30023:<recipeAuthor>:<recipeDTag>` (`NourishParser.kt:104–105`,
frontend `buildNourishDTag` in `nourishRelay.ts:54–56`). An `a` tag
holds the same coordinate (`30023:<pubkey>:<dTag>`). Explore parses
rows from the `a` tag (`NourishDiscovery.kt:188–193`); a missing /
unparseable `a` is skipped.

**Content JSON** (server publishes this; clients parse, never
recompute `overall` — `NourishParser.kt:67–70`):

- 8 dimensions, display order: Real Food, Gut, Protein,
  Anti-Inflammatory, Blood Sugar, Immune, Brain, Heart
  (`NourishParser.kt:90–99`). Each is `{score, label}`; missing dims
  default to **0** (legacy).
- `overall: {score, label}` — **required**; absent → parse returns
  null.
- `improvements`: ≤5 non-blank strings.
- Additive `macros` (prompt v4): `perServing.{kcal,protein_g,carbs_g,fat_g}`,
  `servingsUsed`, `servingsParsed`, `confidence` ∈ {`estimate`,`rough`},
  `method`. Malformed → null row, scores still parse.
- Ignored extras: `promptVersion`, `cacheVersion`, `ingredient_signals`,
  `audience` / `audience_scores`, `labels`, `summary`, `createdAt`.

**Versioning** lives on tags + content, not as a client schema gate.
Frontend today: `NOURISH_CACHE_VERSION = '2.0'`,
`NOURISH_PROMPT_VERSION = '4'` (`types.ts:1–2`). Tags include
`nourish_version`, `prompt_version`, `content_hash`, per-dim
`nourish_*` scores, optional NIP-32 `L`/`l` under namespace
`cooking.zap.nourish` (`nourishPublisher.server.ts:113–150`).
Android's parser never requires those tags; labels are Explore-only.

**How many are read.**

- Single-recipe: `limit = 1` (`NourishRepository.kt:56–61`).
- Explore: `limit = 200` (`NourishDiscovery.kt:162–168`); ranked
  display takes 40 (`NourishExploreViewModel.kt:167–170`).

**Local cache (session only — not ObjectBox, not UserDefaults).**

- Score cache: `ConcurrentHashMap<author:dTag, NourishScore>`
  (`NourishRepository.kt:40, 53–54, 386–388`).
- Explore: 5-minute SWR discovery cache + recipe-event cache
  (`NourishDiscovery.kt:16, 86–87, 221–266`). Never-clobber empty
  revalidate (`NourishDiscovery.kt:147–154`). `clear()` on account
  switch.

---

## 2. The read filter Android sends

### Explore unfiltered (the kitchen-tab destination's first REQ)

`NourishDiscovery.buildNourishAnalysisFilter(null)` at
`NourishDiscovery.kt:162–168` → `NourishRepository.kt:218–219`:

```
kinds   = [30078]
authors = [<SERVICE_PUBKEY>]
limit   = 200
```

No `#d`, no `#l`, no `#t`. This **is** the pinned public shape from
this morning's C-B probe, plus `limit` (narrowing).

### Explore filtered (chip AND)

Same authors/kinds/limit, plus `#l = [<most-selective label>]`
(`NourishDiscovery.kt:164–167`). Remaining labels are client-side
intersect (`NourishDiscovery.kt:181–186`). Extra `#l` is **allowed**
by policy (below).

### Single-recipe (recipe detail, not the kitchen tab)

`NourishRepository.fetchScore` at `NourishRepository.kt:56–61`:

```
kinds   = [30078]
authors = [<SERVICE_PUBKEY>]
#d      = ["nourish:30023:<author>:<dTag>"]
limit   = 1
```

Extra `#d` is **allowed** by policy. Frontend
`queryNourishEvent` (`nourishRelay.ts:105–109`) sends the same
authors/kinds/`#d` without a limit.

### Policy vs the C-B one-liner

member-relay `isPublicNourishFilter` (`relay/main.go:679–703`):

> filter must pin `authors` to **exactly** `[nourishServicePubkey]`
> AND request kind 30078 **exclusively**. Any `#l`/`#d` / limit /
> since/until further **narrow** and never broaden, so they don't
> affect the decision.

The Go test (`relay/main_test.go:39–54`) explicitly allows
`#l` + `#d` + limit + since + until on that pin. Recipes
(kind 30023) are a separate always-public path
(`relay/main.go:708–711`).

**C-B "one extra tag and the read silently fails" overstates the
policy.** Extra tags on a correctly pinned authors+kinds filter are
fine. What AUTH-gates: missing `authors`, extra authors, kinds-less,
or kinds that aren't exclusively 30078.

Android does **not** rely on AUTH for these reads. Comments at
`NourishRepository.kt:42–45` and `213–216` say anonymous service-key
30078 REQs are public; `hasSigningKey` is unused on the read.
`AuthedRelayReader` still *can* AUTH if a key is present, but the
filter shape is what makes the read public. iOS must use
`RelayPool.query`, not `GroupRelayPool`.

---

## 3. Compute: client or backend?

**Backend.** Android does not derive scores on-device from ingredients.

| | |
|---|---|
| Path | `POST https://zap.cooking/api/nourish` |
| Client | long-timeout compute client (~75 s) — `ZapCookingApi.kt:271–308` |
| Auth | **pubkey-in-body, not NIP-98** (`ZapCookingApi.kt:272–273`). iOS `ZapCookingApi.swift:20–22` already documents this. |
| Gate | `requireMembership` fail-closed (`frontend src/routes/api/nourish/membershipCheck.ts:13–59`). `MEMBERSHIP_ENABLED` off → no gate. |
| Non-member | HTTP **403**, body `{ success: false, error: "Premium membership required for Nourish" }` — **no `code` field** (`membershipCheck.ts:46–49`). Android maps **any** 403 → `MembersOnly` (`ZapCookingApi.kt:289`). |
| Success | `{ success, scores, improvements, macros?, … }`. Client parses with `NourishParser.parseScores` + top-level macros; **no pantry re-read**. Server publishes the 30078 to pantry (+ public relays) for everyone else (`+server.ts:94–120`). |
| Frontend twin | `NourishModal.svelte:226–240` — same path, same pubkey-in-body JSON. |

**Not used from Nourish Explore or the kitchen tab.** Compute is
recipe-detail only (`RecipeDetailViewModel.computeNourish`,
`RecipeDetailViewModel.kt:147–180`).

**iOS 0.7a vs Android 403:** `ZapCookingApi.throwErrorIfNeeded`
(`wisp/ZapCookingApi.swift:213–218`) maps a **bare 403 with no
`code`** to `apiRejected`, not `membersOnly`. Nourish's real
non-member body has no `code`. If compute ships, this endpoint needs
an Android-shaped 403 → members-only mapping **without** treating
every 403 in the app as membership denial. Copy must be
`"Nourish scoring is a Zap Cooking members feature."` — never the
server's "Premium membership required" string (purchase-adjacent,
§4.3).

`HttpClientFactory.computeClient` already exists (0.7b). No new
endpoint. NIP-98 is **not** required.

---

## 4. States Android shows (verbatim)

### A. My Kitchen › Nourish tab (`NourishEntrySection`,
`RecipeFeedScreen.kt:1005–1034`, `strings.xml:947–949`)

No loading / empty / member / error. Always the same card, signed-out
included (`CookbookSubTab.NOURISH(false)`, `RecipeFeedScreen.kt:125`):

- emoji **🥦**
- title **Nourish**
- body **See how recipes nourish you — explore the catalog by gut health, protein, heart health, and more.**
- CTA **Explore Nourish**

iOS 3.2 already has this, button disabled
(`wisp/NourishPlaceholderView.swift:7–38`).

### B. Nourish Explore (`NourishExploreScreen.kt`, `strings.xml:987–1001`)

| State | Copy |
|---|---|
| Loading | **Finding analyzed recipes…** |
| Error | **Something went wrong. Please try again.** + button **Retry** |
| Empty | **No analyzed recipes yet.** / **Once recipes are analyzed with Nourish, they'll appear here ranked by their nutrition profile.** |
| Degraded (filter miss → unfiltered fallback) | **More recipes being analyzed — showing the full ranked list for now.** |
| Refreshing (SWR) | **Updating…** |
| Footer (filtered) | **%d recipes matching your filters** |
| Footer (all) | **%d recipes with Nourish profiles** |
| Honesty caption | **AI-generated estimates — guidance, not gospel** |
| Title | **Nourish Explore** |

No members-only. No watch-only. No compute.

### C. Recipe detail (`RecipeDetailViewModel.NourishUi`,
`RecipeDetailScreen.kt:286–300`, `NourishSectionPanels.kt`)

| State | What renders | Copy |
|---|---|---|
| `Loading` | **nothing** | (quiet) |
| `Hidden` | **nothing** | watch-only / no key **and** no published score |
| `Scored` | `NourishCard` | header **Nourish**, **{n}/10**, affirming label only if overall ≥ 5; **What this meal brings**; macros **Estimated per serving** / **Rough estimate** / ` (servings assumed: N)`; **Nourish Profile**; **Simple upgrades**; footer **Profiles are estimates based on ingredients. Not medical advice.** |
| `NotScored` | compute panel | **Nourish** / **See this recipe's Nourish profile across 8 dimensions.** / button **Get Nourish profile** |
| `Computing` | same panel, spinner | **Scoring… (this can take a moment)** |
| `MembersOnly` | message panel | **Nourish scoring is a Zap Cooking members feature.** |
| `Error` | message panel + Retry | Android's `Couldn't compute the Nourish score (N).` / `No score in the response.` / `Couldn't read the Nourish score.` / `Network error — please try again.` |

Dead string, **not shown anywhere**:
`nourish_signing_required` = "Sign in with a key to fetch Nourish
profiles." (`strings.xml:985`). Watch-only on a miss is Hidden, not a
toast. iOS `RecipeSaveGate.needsKey` applies **only if we ship
compute** (a key-required action). The pantry **read** is anonymous.

Card greens (build doc already has these): strong ≥7 `#22C55E`,
moderate 4–6 `#4ADE80`, light 0–3 `#86EFAC`. Soft labels: score 0 →
**Not a focus here**; ≤2 → **Lightly present**. No letter grades.

---

## 5. Does anything in Nourish write?

**The client publishes no Nourish events.** Kind 30078 is signed by
the service key on the server (`nourishPublisher.server.ts`).

- Kitchen tab: navigation only.
- Explore: REQ only; 30023 resolve on article relays.
- Recipe-detail compute: `POST /api/nourish`. Server awaits pantry
  publish, then returns the score. Android `hasSigningKey` is unused
  on the **read**; compute returns early if `signer?.pubkeyHex` is
  nil (`RecipeDetailViewModel.kt:156`).
- `/api/nourish/flag` and `/api/nourish/scan` exist on the frontend.
  **Zero Android call sites.** Do not invent a write/flag/scan path.

**Split:** treat compute as the write-adjacent follow-up (it causes a
server-side 30078 publish). Ship **read** (Explore + recipe-detail
card) first.

---

## 6. Live-gate feasibility

**Read canary — no key.** Open `wss://pantry.zap.cooking` with a raw
(unauthenticated) WebSocket, send the named pinned REQ:

```
["REQ","nourish-live",{"kinds":[30078],"authors":["fdd263f69f9e95a2a0a58ec3e7e8053011214fa66007d93b26d2f4717d31917b"],"limit":200}]
```

Expect: `EVENT`s (kind 30078, that author) and `EOSE`. Assert **no
`AUTH` frame** and no `CLOSED … auth-required`. Sentinel:
`wispTests/.nourish_live_enable` / `NOURISH_LIVE=1`, same opt-in
pattern as `SousChefLiveTests`. This is also the relay-policy canary.

A second hermetic-enough probe can `#d`-pin a known coordinate
(`limit: 1`) — still public per policy.

Do **not** drive the canary through `RelayPool.query` alone:
`RelayConnectionPool` will AUTH-and-replay if a key happens to be in
process (`RelayPool.swift:603–611`), which would hide a policy
regression. Raw socket, no signer.

**Compute (deferred):** a throwaway key can prove the non-member 403
shape (`MembersOnly` copy, no purchase language). Member path is a
manual checklist (`owner: true` on `/api/membership/check-status`).
Not this PR if we ship read first.

**Unexpected AUTH on the product read path** (policy flipped under
us): `RelayPool.query` currently swallows `CLOSED auth-required` and
waits for AUTH (`RelayPool.swift:590–596`). Watch-only never AUTH →
timeout → empty list, which would look like Explore's empty state.
Step 2 must distinguish that from a genuine empty corpus and show
Explore's **error** copy ("Something went wrong. Please try again."),
not the empty copy. Recipe-detail read stays quiet-absence on miss
(Android), but an AUTH challenge is not a miss — surface error there
too if we ship the card.

Issue **#6 does not block**. `RelayPool.query` already re-issues
every REQ after a successful AUTH (`RelayPool.swift:609–611`). #6 is
the `GroupRelayPool` subscribe path. Nourish must not use that pool.
Correct §2 / §7.1 / §8 3.5 / `RelayDefaults.members` comment.

---

## 7. Files to create or modify

New files under `wisp/` / `wispTests/` only — **zero pbxproj**.

### Create

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `wisp/NourishParser.swift` | Port of `NourishParser.kt` (scores, macros, d-tag, service pubkey, clamp, trust stored `overall`) |
| `wisp/NourishDiscovery.swift` | Port of `NourishDiscovery.kt` (chips, selectivity, `#l` intersect, parseAnalyses, sort, session cache) |
| `wisp/NourishRepository.swift` | `RelayPool.query` on `RelayDefaults.members`; pinned corpus filter; optional `#d` fetchScore; 30023 resolve via existing `RecipeRepository` / article relays |
| `wisp/NourishExploreView.swift` | Port of `NourishExploreScreen.kt` |
| `wisp/NourishExploreViewModel.swift` | Port of `NourishExploreViewModel.kt` |
| `wisp/NourishExploreRecipeCard.swift` | Leaf mark + macros snippet (`NourishExploreComponents.kt`) |
| `wisp/NourishCard.swift` | Green-island card (`NourishCard.kt`) for recipe detail |
| `wispTests/NourishParserTests.swift` | Android `NourishParserTest` goldens verbatim |
| `wispTests/NourishDiscoveryTests.swift` | Android `NourishDiscoveryTest` goldens (filter shape, chips, intersect, cache) |
| `wispTests/NourishFilterShapeTests.swift` | Pinned REQ keys ⊆ {`kinds`,`authors`,`limit`}; fails if a tag is added |
| `wispTests/NourishExploreTests.swift` | Loading / empty / error / degraded / kill switch |
| `wispTests/NourishCardTests.swift` | Quiet miss / scored; AUTH-challenge ≠ empty |
| `wispTests/NourishLiveTests.swift` | Opt-in pantry canary |

### Modify

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `wisp/NourishPlaceholderView.swift` | Enable CTA; push Explore when `nourishEnabled` |
| `wisp/MyKitchenView.swift` | `navigationDestination` for Explore; hide tab if kill switch off |
| `wisp/RecipeDetailView.swift` | Render `NourishCard` / quiet miss (read-only this PR) |
| `wisp/RecipeDetailViewModel.swift` | Independent pantry `fetchScore`, Android state machine minus compute |
| `FeatureFlags.swift` | `nourishEnabled = true` |
| `NostrEvent.swift` (`NostrFilter`) | Add `lTags` → `"#l"` so Explore chip REQs encode. Existing file; no pbxproj |
| `RelayDefaults.swift` | Drop the "reads REQUIRE issue #6" comment on `members` |
| `ZAPCOOKING_IOS_BUILD.md` | §2 Nourish (AUTH-on-every-read is false; #6 does not block), §7.1, §8 3.5 + 3.2 hand-off, Phase-order item 11/15 |

### Not this PR (compute follow-up)

`wisp/ZapCookingApi.swift` `computeNourish`, `NourishSectionPanels`
compute/members-only UI, `RecipeSaveGate.needsKey` on **Get Nourish
profile**, 0.7a-vs-bare-403 mapping.

### Do not touch

`GroupRelayPool`, wallet/zap, `Nip98` internals, `RecipePublisher`,
`project.pbxproj`, Grocery, Planner.

---

## Plan changes vs the prompt / the doc

1. **Issue #6 no longer blocks Nourish read.** Use `RelayPool.query`.
   Doc §2 / §7.1 / §8 3.5 / `RelayDefaults.members` are stale.
2. **Pantry 30078 with authors=`[service]` + kinds=`[30078]` is public
   without AUTH.** `#d`/`#l`/limit are allowed narrowing, not a
   silent-fail extra. C-B "one extra tag fails" is overstated vs
   `isPublicNourishFilter`.
3. **Kitchen tab does not read or compute.** It navigates to Explore.
   Explore is the pantry corpus read. Compute is recipe-detail +
   `POST /api/nourish` (pubkey-in-body, member-gated, not NIP-98).
4. **Ship read first** (Explore + recipe-detail card). Defer compute.
5. Watch-only does not need a toast on the read path. `needsKey`
   composes only with compute.
6. Unexpected AUTH on a pinned public REQ is an **error**, not empty.

title: Fix PR 27 review blockers and pin merged Sherpa
body: ## What this fixes This PR carries the proxy-runtime recovery from #27 plus the review blockers on that PR. - Pins `sherpa` to squash-merged Sherpa main `caaf5dbf0f961f11e156d467f74fba5058118be7` (`https://github.com/bitball41/sherpa/archive/caaf5dbf0f961f11e156d467f74fba5058118be7.tar.gz`) with a recomputed `package-lock.json` integrity for that tarball - Proxied pages load Sherpa's client-only bundle (`sherpa.client.js`) as controller `files.all` - The parent chrome and service worker keep loading `sherpa.all.js` (host bundle) for `$sherpaLoadController` / `$sherpaLoadWorker` - Service worker registration waits for the replacement worker to activate. A 15s timeout plus an already-`active` worker is no longer treated as success while a new worker is still installing/waiting - Adds tests for the libcurl Wisp pool: rotate on retryable codes, extra same-session retry on error 7, do not remember a failed egress as preferred, do not replay unsafe POST/body requests, epoxy only after the pool is exhausted ## Already-correct recovery behavior kept from #27 - Retryable curl codes 6/7/28/35/52/56/60 - Session records so in-flight requests survive rotate - Drop `wss://nebulaservices.org/wisp/` - Serialized engine init so a stale startup cannot overwrite a newer selection - `SKIP_WAITING` on `sw.js` / `sw-sherpa.js` ## Checks - `npm ci` succeeds against the new Sherpa tarball and matching lockfile integrity - `npm test` — 72 tests pass - Typecheck + Vite production build pass

title: Fix libcurl could not connect error 7
body: ## What was dying #25 rotated Wisp on libcurl error 60 (bad cert), then **stuck on that public egress**. The next request to the same dest (`https://toustream.xyz/`) came back as: ``` Request failed with error code 7: Could not connect to server at finish_callback (.../libcurl/upstream.mjs:5807:20) ``` `CURLE_COULDNT_CONNECT`. TCP never happened. Two stacked bugs: 1. Error 7 was not retryable — failover only knew about 35/60. 2. A failed rotate became the sticky default, so a dead/blocked public Wisp owned the whole session. `nebulaservices.org` is in the public list and does not even resolve, which is a great way to manufacture error 7. ## Fix - Per-request walk of local → public Wisp on **6 / 7 / 28 / 35 / 60** (resolve, connect, timeout, handshake, cert). - Extra same-egress retry on 7 after a rotate (libcurl will ask before the new WebSocket is up). - Only remember an egress that actually succeeded. Next page load starts from last *good* server, not last *failure*. - Drop `wss://nebulaservices.org/wisp/`. - Cache-bust `?v=1.5.2-e7`. ## Tests `npm test` — 54/54 `npm run typecheck` — clean Production still needs the VPS SSH deploy after merge.

title: Network relay: real TCP/UDP routing over WISP
body:
Closes the routing half of #40: the relay now does real networking instead of logging frames.

## WISP relay
`tools/network-relay.mjs` is a **WISP** relay (Node 22+, no deps). v86 supports `wisp://`, which
runs a TCP/IP stack in the browser — it answers the guest's DHCP and ARP itself — and forwards
each flow as a WISP stream. The relay opens the matching real socket: `node:net` for TCP,
`node:dgram` for UDP so the guest's DNS resolves. No TAP, no root.

**Verified routing real traffic, on loopback:**
- WISP TCP stream to `example.org:80` → `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` came back through the relay.
- WISP UDP stream to `8.8.8.8:53` → a DNS answer came back (68 bytes).

So both TCP and DNS work end to end through the relay.

## App wiring
The app maps the `ws://`/`wss://` URL you enter to `wisp://`/`wisps://` before handing it to
v86, because v86 picks its backend from the scheme. Three unit tests cover the mapping and that a
blank relay adds no network field. 94 tests pass; Android and iOS build clean.

## Honest verification state
- Relay routes real TCP + UDP: **verified** (loopback, above).
- Settings persistence, on/offline state, and the `wisp://` hand-off: **verified** on a Galaxy A34.
- The full phone → relay → internet path from inside the guest is **not** confirmed yet. The
  guest needs several minutes to reach its `udhcpc` stage, the test phone's Wi-Fi had a manual
  HTTP proxy configured, and the run kept being interrupted by the phone being picked up (which
  backgrounds the app and pauses the guest). `emulator/NETWORK-RELAY.md` says exactly this.

The mechanism is complete and proven to route; the remaining item is one uninterrupted on-device
run.

Adds a small Ultraviolet proxy page under `/proxy/` that is compatible with GameVault's existing Netlify static deployment. title: fix: disable loopback IP access in Wisp proxy configuration
body:
## Summary

The Wisp proxy configuration in `src/server.mjs` has `allowLoopbackIPs: true`, which allows any unauthenticated user connected to the proxy to route requests to `127.0.0.1` (and other loopback addresses) on the server. This is a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CWE-918).

## Vulnerability Details

**File:** `src/server.mjs`, line 37
**Configuration:** `allowLoopbackIPs: true` in the `Mrrowisp` constructor
**Severity:** Medium-High
**CWE:** CWE-918 (Server-Side Request Forgery)

InvisiProxy is a public-facing web proxy that requires no authentication. The Wisp protocol handler (`mrrowisp`) accepts WebSocket connections on the `/wisp` upgrade path and proxies TCP connections on behalf of clients. The `allowPrivateIPs: false` setting correctly blocks RFC1918 private ranges, but `allowLoopbackIPs: true` explicitly permits connections to `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, and other loopback addresses.

This means any remote user can reach services listening on localhost of the server — including any service bound to the whitelisted ports (80, 443, 9050, 7000, 7001 as configured in the `whitelistedPorts` array). Depending on what's running on the host, this could expose admin panels, databases, or other sensitive internal services.

## Proof of Concept

A client connects to the publicly exposed Wisp WebSocket endpoint and requests a TCP connection to `127.0.0.1:80`:

```javascript
// Connect to the InvisiProxy Wisp endpoint
// The WebSocket upgrade is handled at the /wisp path (src/server.mjs line 131)
import { WispConnection } from "wisp-js";

const conn = new WispConnection("wss://target-invisiproxy-instance.com/wisp/");
const stream = conn.create_stream("127.0.0.1", 80);
// stream now has a TCP connection to localhost:80 on the server
stream.send(new TextEncoder().encode("GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n"));
// Response from localhost:80 is returned to the attacker via the Wisp stream
```

No authentication is required — the proxy is public-facing and the WebSocket upgrade path has no auth gate (the `upgrade` event handler at line 130-132 routes directly to `wisp.route()` with no credential check).

## Fix

One-line change: set `allowLoopbackIPs: false`. This tells mrrowisp to reject connection requests targeting loopback addresses, matching the existing `allowPrivateIPs: false` policy for RFC1918 ranges.

```diff
-  allowLoopbackIPs: true,
+  allowLoopbackIPs: false,
```

## Testing

- Verified the change is syntactically correct and the configuration option is consistent with the existing `allowPrivateIPs: false` setting.
- After this fix, Wisp clients attempting to connect to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` will be rejected by mrrowisp before a TCP connection is established.
- Legitimate proxy functionality (connecting to external hosts) is unaffected.

## Adversarial Review

Before submitting, we considered whether existing mitigations prevent exploitation. The `whitelistedPorts` array restricts which destination ports are allowed, which limits the blast radius — but ports 80 and 443 on localhost are still reachable, which commonly host admin interfaces, metrics endpoints, or other sensitive services. The `allowPrivateIPs: false` setting shows the maintainer intended to block internal network access, suggesting `allowLoopbackIPs: true` is an oversight rather than an intentional design choice. The server's own console warning (line 368) explicitly mentions "loopbacks" as a security concern with certain reverse proxies, further confirming loopback access should be restricted.

title: XWAH-29: Add a private local WISP relay for appliance networking
body:
## Goal

Add a reproducible, loopback-only local relay for the Ghostty/Codex appliance so normal development and acceptance do not depend on the slower public `wss://relay.widgetry.org/` service.

Keep the appliance HTTP server on port 8082. Expose the relay separately on `127.0.0.1:8083` and launch the appliance with an encoded `wisp://127.0.0.1:8083/` URL.

## Architecture decision

Start with a rootless WISP server rather than a raw-Ethernet wsproxy:

- v86 already implements the WISP client, TCP state machine, and virtual ARP/DHCP/DNS/NTP services;
- Codex, GitHub, and model authentication use outbound HTTPS/WebSocket traffic, so TCP is the required appliance contract;
- WISP avoids TAP devices, dnsmasq, host NAT rules, and privileged Linux networking, which makes a local macOS/Docker Desktop workflow practical.

Raw Ethernet, inbound guest listeners, and UDP application traffic remain outside this ticket. If those become requirements, evaluate RootlessRelay or a Linux VM-backed wsproxy separately.

## Deliverables

- Add a dedicated local-relay project under `tools/` with a pinned WISP implementation, dependency lock, and reviewed checksums or image digest.
- Provide deterministic build, foreground run, health-check, acceptance, and cleanup commands through the root Makefile.
- Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default; never expose an unauthenticated open proxy on all interfaces.
- Validate the WebSocket `Origin` against the local appliance origin and reject non-local browser origins.
- Block loopback, link-local, and private-network destination ranges by default to prevent a browser page from using the relay as a LAN pivot; make any development override explicit.
- Document the launch URL:

  ```text
  http://127.0.0.1:8082/examples/virtio_gpu_codex.html?renderer=wgpu&accelerated=1&relay=wisp%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A8083%2F
  ```

- Keep the public relay as an explicit fallback, not the default local-development path.

## Acceptance

- A clean macOS/Docker Desktop checkout can build and run the relay without TAP/TUN devices, host route changes, or root-owned host files.
- Five consecutive fresh appliance boots obtain a DHCP lease and report `V86_APPLIANCE_NETWORK=PASS` with zero relay-related readiness failures.
- The existing TLS probe to `https://api.github.com/zen` passes through the local relay.
- The accelerated `wgpu` appliance acceptance scenario passes on port 8082 using the local relay.
- A fixed HTTPS workload records connection latency, throughput, and five-run median/p95 against `relay.widgetry.org`; publish the measured improvement and raw results.
- Relay shutdown leaves no background process, container, socket, route, or firewall change behind.
- Logs omit credentials, authorization headers, request bodies, and destination query strings.

## Security boundary

The i386 Codex port does not have its normal Linux network seccomp filter. The local relay therefore narrows transport dependency and improves performance, but it does not replace the appliance's external isolation boundary.

## Non-goals

- Public relay hosting
- Guest inbound port forwarding
- Raw Ethernet/LAN bridging
- General UDP application support
- Persisting Codex credentials in the image

title: Amber with NIP-46 proxy support: message from the notification is missing in the chat
body:
Thanks for building the app, it's awesome!

I'm looking for a way to make DMs in a [safe enough](https://github.com/greenart7c3/Amber/issues/345) way for me. It's [implemented](https://github.com/greenart7c3/Amber/pull/418) in Amber already, not yet merged though.

Here's what's happening, steps to reproduce:

1. Install Amber release build with proxy support

```bash
#!/bin/bash

git clone --depth=1 --revision=d26fafad77e77ad9a72eb138384dac9bd974a98d https://github.com/greenart7c3/Amber # --branch=claude/add-bunker-proxy-login-ciFdm

cd Amber

./gradlew clean bundleRelease --stacktrace
./gradlew assembleRelease --stacktrace

keytool -genkeypair \
-alias amberkey \
-keyalg RSA \
-keysize 2048 \
-validity 10000 \
-keystore release.keystore \
-storepass password \
-keypass password \
-dname "CN=Amber, OU=Dev, O=AmberProject, L=Internet, S=None, C=US"

~/Android/Sdk/build-tools/36.0.0/apksigner sign \
--ks release.keystore \
--ks-key-alias amberkey \
--ks-pass pass:password \
--key-pass pass:password \
--out signed.apk \
./app/build/outputs/apk/free/release/app-free-arm64-v8a-release-unsigned.apk

adb install signed.apk
```

2. Run bunker for a new npub

```bash
#!/bin/bash

export NOSTR_SECRET_KEY=$(nak key generate)

echo '{"kind":10050,"tags":[["relay","wss://relay.ditto.pub"],["relay","wss://auth.nostr1.com"],["relay","wss://chat.wisp.talk"],["relay","wss://relay.dreamith.to"],["relay","wss://relay.nmail.li"]]}' | nak event wss://purplepag.es wss://profiles.nostr1.com

echo "npub: $(echo ${NOSTR_SECRET_KEY} | nak key public | nak encode npub)"
echo "nsec: $(nak encode nsec ${NOSTR_SECRET_KEY})"

nak bunker --qrcode wss://nrs.primal.net wss://bucket.coracle.social
```

3. Scan QR, run Amber - `Login as bunker proxy` - paste the `bunker://` URI
4. Install Nospeak 1.1.3 from Zapstore, run it, `Login with Amber`
5. Login to Nospeak from the desktop browser with another npub using nsec

```bash
#!/bin/bash

export NOSTR_SECRET_KEY=$(nak key generate)

echo '{"kind":10050,"tags":[["relay","wss://relay.ditto.pub"],["relay","wss://auth.nostr1.com"],["relay","wss://chat.wisp.talk"],["relay","wss://relay.dreamith.to"],["relay","wss://relay.nmail.li"]]}' | nak event wss://purplepag.es wss://profiles.nostr1.com

echo "npub: $(echo ${NOSTR_SECRET_KEY} | nak key public | nak encode npub)"
echo "nsec: $(nak encode nsec ${NOSTR_SECRET_KEY})"
```

6. Send a message from desktop to phone, observe the message on the phone
7. Reboot the phone
8. Send another message from desktop while the phone keeps rebooting
9. Unlock the lock screen, open the notifications bar
10. Wait and observe the notification with the expected message body
11. Tap on the notification, observe that the same message from the notification is missing in the chat

Reproduces on the latest GrapheneOS, Pixel 7, no Google Play installed.

title: Define Gate 0-H; correct the 1.1 parser test count to 23
body:
Doc-only. Two corrections to `ZAPCOOKING_IOS_BUILD.md`, both raised by Chief in the ios-app-launch channel.

## 1. §Phase 1 / 1.1 — 14 tests → 23

At `zap_cooking_android` `4389530`, `RecipeParserTest.kt` has **23** `@Test` methods, not 14. Verified by counting at that commit.

The 14 is exactly the block *above* the `private fun event(...)` helper at `:199` — a helper that sits mid-file and reads like the end of it. The 9 below are `isRecipe_*` and `validate_*`, and they are the ones with downstream teeth: `RecipeParser.isRecipe` is the gate **1.6** uses to choose the recipe route over the article route, and `isRecipe_rejectsArticleCarryingRecipeTag` is precisely the case that otherwise lands a plain article on a recipe screen. Port 14 and the gate function ships untested.

The line now pins the source path and the commit, so the count is checkable rather than remembered.

## 2. Gate 0-H — defined (ruling still Seth's)

0-H was blocking Concern 0.4 while existing only in chat. It is now a row in the Gate 0 table and an entry in §9.

The substance, verified in source:

- It is **not** a client-side constant. `RelaySettingsRepository.ensureDmRelayList` (`:113-153`) **signs and publishes a kind-10050 into the member's own account**, once per account, reached at every launch via `MainView.swift:343` → `bootstrap`. A kind-10050 is cross-client and supersedes by `created_at` — whatever we write is where every Nostr client that member uses routes their DMs.
- The value is the inherited Wisp constant `wss://auth.nostr1.com` (`:44`). Its own NIP-11, probed Aug 9: `auth_required: true`, `payment_required: false`, and it describes itself as *"a 'DM Inbox Relay' running alpha software. By using it you can help us test the functionality."*
- **Pantry cannot be the answer.** `rejectEventPolicy` falls through to "membership required" for kind 1059 (`member-relay relay/main.go:511-514` @ `06e70c8`) and a gift-wrap sender AUTHs as an ephemeral key that is never a member — inbound DMs would be rejected.
- Two existing safeguards are sound and should survive any ruling: at most once per account, and only on a connectivity-confirmed absence (`relaysResponded > 0`), so it cannot supersede a real list we merely failed to fetch.

Three decisions, not one: **(a)** do we publish a 10050 on the member's behalf at all, given DMs appear nowhere in §3's P0–P3 list; **(b)** what value; **(c)** at launch or at first use of Messages. Recommendation in the doc is (a) yes / (b) keep for now / (c) move the seed to first use — the record is permanent and cross-client and today we write it before the member has opened Messages once.

The seed is **already live in every build**, so "unruled" is not "not happening".

## 3. Concern 0.4 unblocked

Marked not-blocked-on-0-H, flagged as overridable. The four role-based sets are client-side read-fanout constants; a DM inbox relay is a signed event in the member's account. No 0-H outcome changes any of the four values, and a fifth `dm` case could point at the existing `defaultDmRelay` without knowing the ruling.

---

Also flagged in §9: **§4.2 already carries a written ruling on 0-F** (compile-time `FeatureFlags.zapsOnPosts` kill switch). It needs a confirmation, not a decision.

title: fix: reliable NIP-42 auth for NIP-17 DMs (closes #626)
body: ## Summary Closes #626. Nostria had only partial NIP-42 support: `autoRelayAuth` defaulted off (so `onauth` was never attached), DM `pool.query` paths never opted into AUTH, failed `auth-required` rejects could permanently blacklist inbox relays, and new accounts copied non-AUTH account relays into kind 10050. That combination broke NIP-17 gift wraps (kind 1059) on AUTH-required inbox relays. ### Root cause 1. **Auth gated off by default** — `RelayAuthService.getAuthCallback()` returned `undefined` unless `autoRelayAuth` was enabled. 2. **DM reads skipped AUTH** — messaging used `pool.query` without `{ auth: true }` (unlike NIP-29 which already uses `AUTHED`). 3. **Poisoned relay filter** — publish failures with `auth-required:` were blacklisted even when no AUTH callback was provided. 4. **Bad 10050 defaults + Sync UX** — signup/`setupNostriaRelays` copied account relays into kind 10050; “Sync with Account Relays” could overwrite AUTH inboxes with public write relays. ### What changed - **Force AUTH on DM traffic**: messaging `query`/`subscribe` paths pass `{ auth: true }`; `publishToDmRelays` uses `publishWithTracking(..., { auth: true })`. Forced auth ignores the auto-auth toggle when the account can sign (same pattern as NIP-29 reads). - **`getAuthCallback({ force })` + `filterAuthFailedRelays({ allowAuthRequired })`** so AUTH-gated inbox relays are not dropped when auto-auth is off. - **Do not blacklist** `auth-required`/`restricted` failures unless an AUTH callback was actually used. - **Default `autoRelayAuth: true`** for new installs / missing setting (existing explicit `false` is preserved). - **Auth-friendly default kind 10050** (issue-suggested list, kept separate from account/media defaults): - `wss://auth.nostr1.com/` - `wss://relay.ditto.pub/` - `wss://chat.wisp.talk/` - `wss://relay.dreamith.to/` Note: `auth.nostr1.com` is AUTH-only for *all* events — it is only used for 10050, not media (10051) defaults. - **Removed “Sync with Account Relays”** for message relays (+ related handlers/i18n). Empty state and default-setup now point at AUTH-friendly DM relays instead. ## Verification - Unit tests (vitest/jsdom): `relay-auth.service.spec.ts`, `relay-pool.spec.ts`, `default-dm-relays.spec.ts` — **15/15 passed**. - `nak serve --auth --port 1059`: - publish kind 1059 without `--auth` → `auth-required: event` - publish with `--auth` → success - `nak req` without `--auth` → closed with `auth-required: subscribe` - `nak req --auth` → receives the authenticated event This matches the app wiring: DM publish/subscribe/query now always attach a forced `onauth` callback when signing is available.

title: Fails to send NIP-17 DMs to relays that require NIP-42 auth
body:
Nostria currently sets non-auth relays in the 10050 relay list by default for new accounts, which [nostr.doctor](https://nostr.doctor) predictably flags.

Some NIP-17 clients already support NIP-42 for kind 1059 events, at least [Nospeak](https://github.com/psic4t/nospeak) and [YakiHonne](https://github.com/YakiHonne); I guess [Wisp](https://github.com/barrydeen/wisp/tree/main#supported-nips) and [Amethyst](https://github.com/vitorpamplona/amethyst#supported-features) as well; maybe something else.

It'd be awesome to support the auth in Nostria too, set kind 1059 auth-only relays by default in the list 10050 and remove the "sync with account relays" button (since this may set relays that don't require NIP-42 auth for kind 1059).

These are probably the most reliable public relays (the first one is auth-only for all events, so it's not suitable for kind 1005**1**):

```
wss://auth.nostr1.com
wss://relay.ditto.pub
wss://chat.wisp.talk
wss://relay.dreamith.to
```

There's also `wss://relay.nmail.li` (probably less reliable) and `wss://basspistol.org/inbox` (with WoT filtering, not sure if it's good for new accounts that only send kind 1059).

Just in case, recent `nak` received a reference auth relay implementation for debugging (`nak serve --auth` and `nak serve --eager-auth`).

title: Reduce proxy fingerprints so content-filter extensions don't classify the host as a "web proxy"
body:
## Why

Managed-device content-filter extensions block the deployed host by matching a small set of well-known fingerprints of Scramjet-family proxies (URL prefix, base64url path payload, `/wisp/` websocket, `/assets/{app,core}.*` asset tuple, document title of the target). Once a host trips the "web proxy / anonymizer" category, per-target allowlisting no longer helps because category classification wins over hostname allowlists in default policies.

This change rewrites each of those fingerprints so the deployed tuple no longer matches the default rules. It is not a bypass against a determined operator — an extension with full DOM/webRequest access can still iterate — but it defeats the current pattern-based rules that trigger the block for you today.

## What changed

**URL prefix** — `/a/` → `/static/render/` (`packages/controller/src/index.ts`).

**URL codec** — plain base64url (`btoa` → URL-safe swap) → XOR with a fixed 8-byte key then hex-encode (`packages/controller/src/index.ts`). The path no longer decodes to a URL via `atob(location.pathname)`, so classifiers that sniff for a base64-decoded URL come up empty. Output looks like an opaque session token (lowercase hex), not URL-safe base64. Key is a constant baked into both encode and decode; it's not a secret, it just breaks the naive decoder path.

**Websocket endpoint** — `/wisp/` → `/api/socket/`, overridable via `WISP_PATH` env var (`render-server.mjs`, `render.yaml`, `render-build.sh`, `packages/bootstrap/src/common.ts`, `packages/bootstrap/src/server.ts`).

**Asset paths** — `/assets/{app,core}.*` → `/static/chunks/{main,runtime}.*` (`packages/bootstrap/src/common.ts`, `packages/demo/vite.config.ts`, `packages/demo/index.html`, `packages/demo/public/sw.js`, `packages/demo/src/index.tsx`). The vite copy step renames files in lockstep. The `/assets/{app,core}` tuple is the fingerprint filters use to catch mercuryworkshop-family proxies; the new names look like a standard bundled SPA.

**`<title>` spoofing** — new `AkConfig.spoofedTitle` field, default `"Console"`:
- Server-side: HTML rewriter in `packages/core/src/shared/rewriters/html.ts` replaces the `<title>` element's text before it reaches the browser.
- Client-side: new `Document.prototype.title` trap in `packages/core/src/client/dom/document.ts` — reads always return the spoof, writes are swallowed.
- Empty string disables both sides.
Extensions that categorize a tab by its document title (a common content-filter path) now see `"Console"` instead of the target's real title.

**Demo strings** — `<title>Workspace</title>` → `<title>Console</title>` in `packages/demo/index.html` and `packages/demo/src/pages/homepage.html`. "Workspace" is a well-known K-12 proxy landing-page name.

**Default home URL** — `"https://google.com"` → `""` (`packages/demo/src/store.ts`). Auto-populating a well-known hostname in the URL bar is a hint that this is a proxy landing page. `normalizeHomeUrl` now accepts empty and the omnibox no-ops on an empty submit.

**Runway harness pin** — `packages/runway/src/harness/scramjet/public/index.html` now explicitly sets `prefix: "/a/"` so its adversarial URL-leak tests (which grep for `/a/`) keep working regardless of what the default becomes.

**Config knobs**
- `AkConfig.spoofedTitle: string` — set to `""` to disable title spoofing, any non-empty string to freeze the title to that value.
- `WISP_PATH` env var — rotate the websocket path per deployment if a specific value gets flagged. Applies to both build and runtime.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm install && pnpm exec rspack build --mode production` — all packages build clean, no TS errors from the new `spoofedTitle` field on `AkConfig`.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mercuryworkshop/scramjet-demo build` — vite copies files to `dist/static/chunks/` with the new names; grep `dist/` for `/assets/app.` and `/assets/core.` — should be zero hits.
- [ ] Deploy to Render and open a proxied page:
  - URL bar shows `/static/render/<hex>` for the frame prefix, not `/a/<base64>`.
  - Browser tab title reads `"Console"` regardless of the target site's title.
  - Websocket goes to `wss://<host>/api/socket/`, not `/wisp/`.
- [ ] Runway harness adversarial tests still pass (they rely on `prefix: "/a/"` which the harness now pins explicitly).
- [ ] Test empty URL-bar submit on the demo — should no-op instead of navigating to `https://`.

## Not in this PR

The user's writeup also called out several deeper wins that this diff does not attempt: server-side URL indirection (opaque session IDs mapped to real URLs on the server), aggressive minification / string-replacement of `"scramjet"` in the runtime bundle, and randomizing the `$akController` global. Those are larger changes that touch the whole runtime — worth doing next if a deployment still gets flagged after this pass.

title: Add free single-service Render deployment (demo + Wisp backend)
body:
## What this does

Adds everything needed to host Scramjet on Render's **free** plan as a single web service. The demo static site and the Wisp WebSocket backend run on the **same origin**, so the demo connects to `wss://<host>/wisp/` with no CORS and no manually-configured URL.

## Why one service

Scramjet is a proxy, not a CRUD app. It has two parts: a static frontend (HTML/JS + service worker + a Rust→WASM URL rewriter, all running in the browser) and a Wisp server (a WebSocket the browser tunnels TCP through). Serving both from one origin keeps the setup to a single free service and lets the Wisp URL be derived automatically from Render's `RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME` — the demo bakes `VITE_WISP_URL` at build time, and it must be a `wss://` URL on an HTTPS site.

## Changes

- **`render-server.mjs`** — production server: serves `packages/demo/dist` and routes `/wisp/` WebSocket upgrades into the Wisp server. Leaves private/loopback IP access at its safe (disabled) defaults so the proxy can't reach the host's internal network.
- **`render-build.sh`** — installs the Rust nightly toolchain, `wasm-bindgen` 0.2.105, `wasm-opt`, and the `wasm-snip` fork (prebuilt binaries where possible), then builds the rewriter, the rspack bundles, and the static demo. Deliberately skips the slow release `wasm-opt` pass to keep build time reasonable; the WASM is larger but functionally identical.
- **`render.yaml`** — one-click Render Blueprint for the free web service.
- **`DEPLOY-RENDER.md`** — step-by-step walkthrough, free-tier caveats (spin-down, 750 instance-hours, 100 GB egress), troubleshooting, custom domains, and the two-service alternative.
- **`package.json`** — adds `express` and `@mercuryworkshop/wisp-js` as runtime deps plus a `start` script; **`pnpm-lock.yaml`** updated to match.

## Notes

- First build takes ~10–20 min because it compiles the Rust rewriter to WASM.
- Nothing in the existing dev workflow (`pnpm dev`, tests, package layout) changes — this only adds deployment files and two dependencies.

title: fix(nip29): scope group membership to the relay, not the bare group id
body:
NIP-29 group ids are relay-scoped, and short ones (`nostrord`, `lotus`) exist on several relays. Everything that answered "am I in this group, and who runs it" matched on the bare id, so two independent groups were treated as one. Reported from a real account that is a member of `nostrord` on both `wss://chat.wisp.talk` and `wss://groups.0xchat.com`, and an admin of only the first.

Membership now answers per (relay, id) everywhere. The flat bare-id maps are still there for callers with no relay in hand, but they are trusted for a group only while no other relay has served that id.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Group joined on the relay never reached kind:10009, no rail entry | `registerExternalAdd` skipped the invite when the id was joined on ANY relay | the guard, the left-marker self-heal and the invite bookkeeping all match on the invite's own relay |
| Approving the invite card did nothing, and the card was gone | the pending entry was discarded BEFORE adopting, so any guard that blocked the adoption spent the consent | the adoption drops the entry only once the membership is in the joined set, and clears the leave intent for that (relay, group) since an explicit accept IS the user's decision |
| Admin UI and 21 join requests shown on a group the account does not administer | the per-relay member/admin/role mirrors fell back to the flat map while the host relay was cold | the flat value is trusted only while no other relay has served the id; otherwise the entry reads absent until this relay answers |
| Info modal offered only Leave; "Joined" badges wrong on discovery cards | flat id checks in both UIs | `GroupViewModel.isJoinedHere` (consumed by Compose and web) and `Map.isJoinedOn(relay, id)` on every card |

Relay-side membership and the account's own list are separate states, so a missed prompt no longer strands a group: `canAddToMyList` detects "the relay lists me, my kind:10009 does not" and both headers offer **Add to my groups**. Native also stops conflating the two, with participation (composer, Join) following the relay's member list like the web `canPost` while Leave follows the list entry.

Five new tests in `GroupViewModelTest` and `GroupExternalMembershipAdoptionTest` (relay-scoped isJoinedHere/pendingInvite, admins not inherited, invite spent only by the adoption, manual add). One existing test changed: it asserted the member-list fallback this PR removes. 758 pass, plus `compileKotlinJvm` and `compileKotlinJs`.

Known residue, not in this PR: `getRelayForGroup` still resolves through a global hint keyed by bare id, which the most recently constructed `GroupViewModel` overwrites, and the in-memory left/dropped markers are still id-keyed.

- 6b0a5fb4 fix(nip29): scope group membership to the relay, not the bare group id

title: feat: add Feishu and WeChat IM channels
body:
## Problem

You can only talk to a wisp-science workspace agent while sitting at the desktop app. This PR adds IM channel bridging (parity with phantty's 飞书/微信 capability): message a Feishu bot or your WeChat iLink bot and the agent runs the turn at home, replying back into the chat — kick off analyses and check on long-running work from your phone.

## What's included

**Backend — new `src-tauri/src/channels/` module**
- `feishu.rs`: self-built-app bot over Feishu's official long connection (endpoint discovery → WSS → pbbp2 frames → ACK ≤3s), so no public callback URL is required. REST side: cached `tenant_access_token`, text send, bot info. p2p direct, group only when @-mentioned (bot open_id match, placeholder stripping), `event_id` dedupe, auto-reconnect.
- `pbbp2.rs`: hand-rolled protobuf codec for the single long-connection frame message (no prost dependency), round-trip tested.
- `weixin.rs`: official iLink bot API — QR-scan binding yields the bot token, `getupdates` cursor long-poll, text replies. Scanning account is the owner (only its 1:1 messages handled); `errcode -14` (session expired) disables the channel with a re-scan prompt.
- `mod.rs`: `ChannelManager` (start/stop/status, autostart), chat↔session-frame map, `/help` `/new` `/stop` chat commands, 6 Tauri commands.

**Integration**: inbound text reuses the existing `send_message` native-turn path unchanged, so history persistence, tools, MCP, and approvals behave identically and the conversation is visible in the app. Secrets (Feishu app secret, WeChat bot token) go to the OS keyring; non-secret config to SQLite settings.

**Frontend**: Settings → Channels pane (`ui/src/channels_view.rs`, self-contained Leptos component — no `SettingsViewState` plumbing), En/Zh i18n, QR image rendered backend-side as SVG data URL. Mock cases in `ui/mock-bridge.js` and `ui-tests/tests/mock-tauri.ts`.

**New dependencies**: `tokio-tungstenite` (rustls), `qrcode` (svg-only) — both in `src-tauri` only.

## Tests

- 15 new unit tests: pbbp2 round-trip/truncation, Feishu event normalization (p2p/group-@/self-echo/dedupe), weixin filtering + text extraction, reply truncation, QR SVG. `cargo test --workspace`: 209 passed.
- New Playwright test (feishu save args, WeChat QR bind → confirmed → unbind); full suite: 130 passed.
- Manual smoke: mock-mode walkthrough of the pane in En and Zh (screenshots verified), bind flow and status transitions.

## Manual smoke steps

1. Settings → Channels → fill Feishu App ID/Secret (self-built app with long-connection subscription of `im.message.receive_v1`), toggle on, DM the bot.
2. WeChat: Scan to bind → confirm in WeChat → toggle on → message the bot; `/help`, `/new`, `/stop`.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- Text-only v1: no streaming cards, approval buttons, or file transfer (phantty's advanced tier) — approvals still surface in the desktop UI, so unattended turns needing approval wait there.
- Feishu CN domain only (no Lark International yet).
- WeChat replies are bound by the server-side ~30 min `context_token` window; a later message fetches the finished result.
- Live-tenant E2E (real Feishu app / WeChat scan) not run here — protocol shapes mirror phantty's field-tested implementation and the official Go SDK.

title: Land spider TLS fixes via upstream, then repoint (no fork)
body:
Tracking issue for getting the two spider wss/TLS fixes into wisp **through upstream** (karlseguin), so wisp never pins a privkeyio fork. Supersedes the fork-pin PRs #146 and #147 (closed).

## 1. TLS read busy-spin (#145)

Quiet wss upstream relays busy-spin a core: the TLS read loop retried `stream()` on a 0-plaintext control record without re-polling.

**Already fixed upstream.** websocket.zig master `7afc284` ("Improve Client read over TLS") independently moved the poll inside the loop (`pollReadable()`), which kills the spin. No fork or fix-PR needed — wisp just needs to move its websocket pin to `7afc284`+.

- [ ] **karlseguin/http.zig#218** — bump http.zig's websocket pin `99df0d3 -> 7afc284` (dedup: wisp pins websocket directly *and* via http.zig; the two must match).
- [ ] wisp: repoint `websocket` + `httpz` to the new upstream commits. Close #145.
- [ ] (optional) small upstream hardening PR on top of `7afc284`: also gate on the ciphertext buffer so a coalesced data record isn't deferred, and bound zero-plaintext retries against a control-record flood. Nice-to-have, not required to stop the spin.

## 2. Unbounded connect / TLS handshake (#140, option a)

`Client.init` did an unbounded TCP connect + TLS handshake; a blackholed/stalling relay hangs the spider thread in `init()`, blocking shutdown past StartOS's 60s grace -> SIGKILL.

- [ ] **karlseguin/websocket.zig#108** — adds `connect_timeout_ms` (default 10s), bounding connect (non-blocking + poll, single monotonic deadline across addresses) and the handshake (watchdog). Does NOT bound DNS (uncancellable in std); #140 stays open for the DNS residual + option b.
- [ ] Verify shutdown-vs-stalling-relay behavior on the StartOS box (can't be exercised in the build env).
- [ ] Once karlseguin/websocket.zig#108 merges: another http.zig websocket-pin bump, then wisp repoints. 

## Repoint order

Because of the dedup constraint, each websocket move needs http.zig's websocket pin bumped first, then wisp repoints both. Wait for the upstream merges before opening the wisp repoint PR(s) - no fork pins in wisp.

Related: #140, #145.

title: Advertise NIP-17/51 support for kind 10050 (DM Relays List) — Haven/Marmot compat
body:
## Summary

Kind `10050` (NIP-17 DM Relays List) is the replaceable event a user publishes to advertise which relays they want to receive gift-wrapped (`kind:1059`) private DMs on. The [Haven mobile app](https://github.com/mehmetefeumit/Haven-App) publishes and reads these against Wisp for its NIP-17 / Marmot messaging. Structure: replaceable, empty `content`, tags of the form `["relay", "wss://..."]` (NIP-17 §Publishing, NIP-51).

## Investigation — this already works today

Kind `10050` is in the NIP-16 replaceable range (10000–19999) and is handled generically, with no per-kind special casing:

- Classification: `10000 <= kind < 20000` → `replaceable` (`nostr` lib `src/event.zig` `Kind.classify`, used by `kindType`).
- Ingest gate: the only kind-based check on EVENT is the opt-in NIP-86 allowlist `isKindAllowed()` (`src/handler.zig:259`), which returns `true` for every kind unless an operator has explicitly populated an allowlist (`src/management_store.zig:256-262`). There is **no** hardcoded kind denylist.
- Storage: `storeInTxn` routes `replaceable`/`addressable` through `handleReplaceable` (`src/store.zig:97-104`), which keys by `pubkey || kind_be` for replaceable events (`nostr` lib `src/replaceable.zig` `buildKey`, no `d` tag for replaceable) and keeps latest-wins by `created_at`/id (`shouldReplace`). So Wisp stores exactly one `10050` per `(pubkey, kind)` — correct NIP-16 behavior.
- Query: REQ `{kinds:[10050], authors:[...]}` resolves through the generic `idx_kind` / `idx_pubkey` indexes (`src/store.zig:527-551`, `147-160`); nothing filters `10050` out.

**Verdict: acceptance, replaceable storage, and querying of `10050` all work generically today.** The only real gap is advertising/documentation.

## Actual change requested

- Advertise NIP-17 (and NIP-51, which defines the list) in NIP-11 `supported_nips` (`src/nip11.zig:44`, currently `[1,2,9,11,13,16,33,40,42,45,50,65,70,77,86]`).
- Add NIP-17/51 to the supported-NIPs line in `README.md:44`.
- Add an integration assertion in `tests/integration.sh` mirroring the existing NIP-16 replaceable block (`tests/integration.sh:66-73`): publish two `10050` events with `relay` tags, assert a single stored event and latest-wins.

Note: NIP-17 also says relays SHOULD serve `kind:1059` only to the p-tagged recipient under NIP-42 AUTH. That is a separate privacy hardening item, out of scope here.

title: Document kind 10051 (Marmot KeyPackage Relays List) support — Haven/Marmot compat
body:
## Summary

Kind `10051` (KeyPackage Relays List, Marmot / MIP-00) is the replaceable event a user publishes to advertise which relays host their MLS `KeyPackage` events. The [Haven mobile app](https://github.com/mehmetefeumit/Haven-App) maps `RelayType::KeyPackage → Kind::MlsKeyPackageRelays (10051)` (`haven-core/src/circle/relay_prefs.rs`) and publishes/reads it against Wisp. Same structure as `10050`: replaceable, empty `content`, `["relay", "wss://..."]` tags.

## Related kinds Haven also puts on the relay

For context (all already handled generically by Wisp, see below):
- `30443` — canonical KeyPackage, **addressable** (30000–39999), keyed by `(pubkey, kind, d)`.
- `443` — legacy KeyPackage twin, **regular** event, stored as-is.
- `1059` — gift-wrapped DM, regular.

## Investigation — this already works today

Kind `10051` is in the NIP-16 replaceable range (10000–19999), handled generically with no special casing:

- Classification: `10000 <= kind < 20000` → `replaceable` (`nostr` lib `src/event.zig` `Kind.classify`).
- Ingest gate: only the opt-in allowlist `isKindAllowed()` (`src/handler.zig:259`); default-allow, no hardcoded denylist (`src/management_store.zig:256-262`).
- Storage: replaceable path in `handleReplaceable` keys by `pubkey || kind_be` and keeps latest per `(pubkey, kind)` (`src/store.zig:97-104`, `118-145`; `nostr` lib `src/replaceable.zig`).
- Query: REQ `{kinds:[10051], authors:[...]}` served via generic `idx_kind`/`idx_pubkey` (`src/store.zig:527-551`).
- The companion `30443` (addressable) and `443`/`1059` (regular) kinds likewise take generic paths and are stored/served correctly.

**Verdict: acceptance, replaceable storage, and querying of `10051` all work generically today.** No relay code change is required for correctness.

## Actual change requested

`10051` is defined by the Marmot protocol (MIP-00), not a registered NIP, so there is nothing to add to NIP-11 `supported_nips` for it. Remaining work is documentation only:

- Note Marmot/MLS relay-list (`10051`) and KeyPackage (`30443`/`443`) support in `README.md` alongside the supported-NIPs list, so integrators know Wisp stores and serves them as replaceable/addressable/regular events.
- Optional: add an integration assertion in `tests/integration.sh` (mirroring `tests/integration.sh:66-73`) publishing two `10051` events with `relay` tags and asserting single-stored + latest-wins, plus a `30443` addressable check keyed by `d` tag.

title: Release v0.5.12 (spider TLS busy-spin + connect/handshake timeout)
body:
Repoints websocket.zig `99df0d3 -> b70e733` and http.zig `86a44b6 -> 01dc094` (which pins the same websocket), picking up two spider fixes that are now fully upstream. No fork.

### Fixed
- **Busy-spin (#145):** quiet `wss://` upstreams no longer pin a core. The TLS read loop retried on 0-plaintext control records without re-polling; upstream websocket.zig now re-polls inside the loop so a quiet socket parks.
- **Connect/handshake hang (#148 / #140 option a):** spider connect + TLS handshake are now bounded (`connect_timeout_ms`, default 10s each), so a blackholed/stalling relay can't hang the spider thread through shutdown and trigger a SIGKILL past the grace period. Bounds connect+handshake, not DNS (#140 tracks the residual).

Both fixes merged upstream: websocket.zig #103/#108, http.zig websocket-pin bumps #218/#219. Dedup verified (websocket `b70e733` resolves once), build + unit tests pass, boots clean.

Closes #145.

title: docs: multi-geo OPRF quorum bring-up runbook + geo gotchas + relay transport decision
body:
## Multi-geo OPRF quorum bring-up runbook (Phase 5) + geo gotchas

Builds out `docs/hardware.md` Phase 5, which was a thin two-bullet placeholder, into a concrete runbook for standing up the OPRF threshold quorum with a **holder in a different physical location** (the real target: a holder a local theft of the box cannot also seize). Prep for the imminent hardware validation (keep-node-ekzm).

### What's added

- **Phase 5 rewrite** , role-based, step-by-step: generate the group + hand out shares out-of-band (5a); choose the coordination relay (5b); attestation bootstrap (5c); provision the quorum (5d); validate the threshold across a reboot *and* across the geo split (5e); rehearse the duress path across geos (5f). Every command is grounded in the actual `keep frost …` surface the OPRF/duress tests exercise.
- **The relay-transport decision, stated honestly** (5b). The quorum needs one relay both sites reach. A reachable `wss://` relay works today; routing over the on-box mesh `wisp` (most private) is **not wired yet** , keep rejects a raw mesh-IP relay URL (SSRF guard) and the mesh has no name resolver, so there's no address to point `--relay` at. This is the open transport-hardening item (keep-node-3tgp) to settle *during* bring-up rather than guess at. Recommends the reachable-`wss://` path for the first run, with the documented traffic-shape residual.
- **Multi-geo gotchas** , the real-world failures QEMU can't surface: NTP clock sync (events die outside the 300s replay window / 30s future-skew bound, and the duress beacon rides the same window); the mesh underlay needs a routable `selfEndpoint` per node (nvpn refuses RFC1918, no STUN, so a NAT'd remote box must port-forward 51820/udp); both sites must reach the same relay; the remote holder is a full trust-bearing party.

Docs-only; no code/behavior change. Written strictly to shipped behavior and verified against the modules (`frost-gate.nix`, `mesh.nix`, `wisp.nix`) and keep v0.7.1 (relay-URL SSRF guard, replay/skew constants, duress flow). `book/` is a gitignored build artifact, so no rendered HTML to update.

title: [BUG] Query-stream use-after-free on shutdown: httpz Worker.deinit frees thread pool without joining in-flight handlers
body:
## Summary

A WebSocket REQ query racing daemon shutdown can segfault (SIGABRT) inside the query/filter read path. Observed in production on wss://relay1.privkey.io (v0.5.5), triggered when a `/backup/create` (SIGTERM) shutdown landed while a query result stream was still iterating the store.

## Crash signature

```
Segmentation fault
nostr-0.3.6 .../filter.zig:285:10 in filtersMatch
src/store.zig:672:56 in processEntry
src/store.zig:633:38 in next
src/handler.zig:26:21 in streamQueryResults
src/handler.zig:519:40 in handleReq
src/handler.zig:207:35 in handle
signal: 6 (SIGABRT)
```

## Root cause

The WS message handler (`processWebsocketData` → `dataAvailable` → `WsConn.clientMessage` → `Handler.handleReq` → `streamQueryResults` (`handler.zig:25-34`) → `QueryIterator.next`/`processEntry`/`filtersMatch` (`store.zig:633`/`:672`)) runs on httpz's thread pool.

On shutdown, the vendored httpz `Worker(WSH).deinit()` (worker.zig) calls `thread_pool.deinit()`, which **only frees the arena** and never calls `thread_pool.stop()` (the function that sets `stopped`, wakes workers, and joins them). So `listen()` returns while a handler may still be mid-query. `main` then proceeds through its defers to `store.deinit()` / `lmdb.deinit()` (`mdb_env_close`), and the in-flight LMDB read txn segfaults inside `filtersMatch`/`processEntry`. The timing (SIGTERM during a backup) matches exactly.

## Fix (requires vendored httpz fork + build.zig.zon bump)

In `src/worker.zig`, `Worker(WSH).deinit()` must drain the pool before freeing it:

```zig
pub fn deinit(self: *Self) void {
    const allocator = self.allocator;
    self.websocket.deinit();
    allocator.destroy(self.websocket);
    self.thread_pool.stop();   // join in-flight handlers before freeing
    self.thread_pool.deinit();
    ...
```

`stop()` is idempotent, and by `deinit` time the epoll loop has already returned, so this cleanly joins handler threads — guaranteeing no query is in flight when wisp tears down the store/LMDB. Then bump the `httpz` pin in `build.zig.zon`.

A pure-wisp mitigation is **not** sufficient: the handler's input buffer and stack live in thread-pool memory that `deinit` frees, so a wisp-side in-flight counter can't prevent the UAF. The fix belongs in httpz.

## Notes

- Still present on the current pinned upstream (`karlseguin/http.zig@5d1b4e2e`); the v0.5.5 repoint did not address this path.
- Distinct from the `worker.zig getState` use-after-free (Crash A), which the upstream repoint already fixed.

title: Fix spider TLS read panic by polling for read readiness (#104)
body:
Closes #104.

## The crash

Building wisp with default `zig build` (debug) and running spider against live `wss://` relays core-dumps mid-sync:

```
thread panic: programmer bug caused syscall error: AGAIN
... std/Io/Threaded.zig netReadPosix .AGAIN => errnoBug
... std/crypto/tls/Client.zig stream
... websocket .../client.zig:447 read
... spider.zig readLoop
```

## Root cause

The spider sets a 1s read timeout (`SO_RCVTIMEO`) on its websocket client so the read loop can poll for shutdown / follow-list changes. On a plaintext (`ws://`) socket a timeout returns `EAGAIN` which websocket.zig's own posix wrapper maps to `error.WouldBlock` (handled as "no message"). But on a `wss://`/TLS socket the read goes through `std.crypto.tls`, whose `std` reader treats `EAGAIN` as a programmer bug and `std.debug.panic`s in debug builds (in ReleaseFast it returns an error and the connection just churns, which is why the shipped s9pk did not crash but reconnected constantly).

Both strfry (uWebSockets/epoll) and nostr-rs-relay (tokio) use readiness-based reads and never hit this.

## Fix

In websocket.zig's client `Stream`, implement the read timeout by **polling the fd for readiness** instead of `SO_RCVTIMEO`: a timeout surfaces as `error.WouldBlock` without ever issuing a read that can `EAGAIN`. The lib drains its own buffer before reaching the socket read, so polling only gates an actual socket read (no buffered-message hazard).

The fix lives in a websocket.zig fork (privkeyio/websocket.zig `fix/tls-read-timeout-poll`, upstream PR: https://github.com/karlseguin/websocket.zig/pull/103). Because http.zig also depends on websocket.zig, its pin is bumped to the same fork so the two `websocket` packages dedupe; this re-pins httpz to a privkeyio/http.zig fork = upstream `80a76dd` with only that websocket bump. Both repoint to upstream once the websocket fix lands.

## Verification

- The exact repro (debug build + spider vs live relays) that core-dumped within seconds now runs cleanly: **no panic**, and connections stay open far longer (one synced 1926 events over **109 s**, vs ~20 s before — the timeout now works instead of tearing the connection down, which also fixes the reconnect churn from #97/#100).
- `zig build test`, protocol suite 36/36 (exercises the httpz-fork relay server), spider suite 3/3.

title: Spider: upstream connections drop with error.ReadFailed and back off aggressively
body:
## Observed

Running wisp as a personal relay against real upstreams (`--spider-admin <npub>` with the default relays damus/nos.lol/nostr.band, 193-pubkey contact list), the initial sync works well: thousands of events are stored (nos.lol 5000, damus 2800). But each upstream connection then fails:

```
info(spider): wss://nos.lol: Stored 5000 events
error(spider): wss://nos.lol: Read error: error.ReadFailed
warning(spider): wss://nos.lol: Quick disconnect after 16358ms, waiting 20000ms
info(spider): wss://nos.lol: Connected (TLS)
error(spider): wss://nos.lol: Read error: error.ReadFailed
warning(spider): wss://nos.lol: Quick disconnect after 20683ms, waiting 40000ms
```

The backoff grows (20s -> 40s ...) on repeated quick disconnects, so after the initial burst the relay maintains only sparse, flaky connections to upstreams. A 193-pubkey sub also trips "Too many pubkeys for negentropy, skipping initial sync", falling back to 10 REQ subscription batches.

## Questions to resolve

- Is `error.ReadFailed` the upstream closing the connection (rate limit / sub cap / idle close on damus/nos.lol) or a wisp WS read-loop issue (read timeout, ping/pong, large-stream buffering)?
- The growing backoff treats a normal post-EOSE close as a failure. Should a clean close after a completed sync reset the backoff instead of escalating it?
- Should the spider keep a steady live subscription open after the historical sync to receive new notes, separate from the periodic re-sync?

## Impact

Not a data-loss issue, the feed does populate and periodic re-sync keeps it current. But choppy upstream connections mean live notes can lag by the backoff window. Found while validating the real-user feed-pull experience for v1.

title: fix(dms): align gift-wrap fetch and survive AUTH-required CLOSED
body:
## Summary
- Stop killing long-lived relay subscriptions on the pre-AUTH `auth-required` CLOSED frame that NIP-42 relays (auth.nostr1.com, inbox.nostr.wine, …) send before / alongside their AUTH challenge. The AUTH branch now runs reliably and replays the REQ on the same socket regardless of frame ordering. Fix applies to both `RelayPool.subscribe` variants (simple and outbox-routed).
- Drop `MessagesViewModel.backfillHistory`. It paginated through `RelayPool.query`, which terminates 1.5 s after any single relay EOSEs — slow / heavy DM-inbox relays were silently cut off mid-stream, and a single short page falsely tripped the "you've got everything" exit. Given randomized gift-wrap timestamps the only correct fetch is one persistent unbounded REQ. Mirrors Android.
- Re-issue the gift-wrap REQ on every live socket every 3 minutes to defeat silent server-side subscription drops, mirroring Android's `subscribeDmsAndNotifications` refresh loop. `RelaySubscription` now tracks its open sockets and stores the REQ text so refresh can reach them.
- Narrow `resolveDmSubscriptionRelays` to the user's kind-10050 DM relays, falling back to NIP-65 inbox/read relays only when none are set. No write relays, no hardcoded defaults.

title: fix(nip46): include relay.powr.build in default nostrconnect relays

## Summary
- Clave's notification proxy maintains an always-on subscription to `relay.powr.build` (its \"PRIMARY\" path), shared across every paired client. Listing the relay in wisp's nostrconnect URI lets Clave publish the connect ack via that hot socket and skip its secondary-pool code path entirely (which requires `/pair-client` setup, ref-count bookkeeping, and L1 reconnection — collectively the dominant source of intermittent nostrconnect handshake flakiness reported against Clave today).
- `relay.primal.net` stays first in the order, preserving the Primal-iOS-subscribes-to-the-first-relay quirk that motivated the existing comment.
- Other signers ignore unfamiliar relays in the URI, so this is purely additive — Primal/Amber/etc. behavior is unchanged.

## Reproduction (before this fix)
Connect via nostrconnect with Clave: handshake intermittently times out at 180s on the listener side, requiring 2–3 retries. After approving in Clave, the connect ack sometimes never reaches wisp's relay subscription. Symptom is sensitive to whether Clave can establish a fresh connection through its secondary-pool path on the URI's relays.

## Verification
Real-world test on iPhone 17 against a production Clave instance: previously-intermittent handshake connected on the first attempt every time after this change.

Proxy-side compliance logs confirm Clave is now publishing via the PRIMARY path:
```
[Compliance] source=wss://relay.powr.build class=PRIMARY client=d4a1821a... event=718f577a...

vs. the previous SECONDARY-class publishes on `nos.lol` / `damus.io`.

title: chore(proxy): evict permanently-failing relays from secondary pool
body:
## Summary

Adds a `maxFailuresWithoutSuccess` threshold to the relay pool's reconnect loop so relays that are permanently broken from this proxy's perspective (e.g. `wss://nostr.wine` 403 / NIP-42-AUTH-required, `wss://garden.zap.cooking/` 502 / down-for-months) are released from active reconnection after N failures with zero successful opens.

## Why now

Inspecting the proxy state during today's Wisp diagnostic session surfaced two stale entries with 500+ cumulative failures each:

```
[RelayPool] wss://nostr.wine/         error: Unexpected server response: 403
[RelayPool] wss://nostr.wine/         reconnecting in 600000ms (failures=534)
[RelayPool] wss://garden.zap.cooking/ error: Unexpected server response: 502
[RelayPool] wss://garden.zap.cooking/ reconnecting in 600000ms (failures=533)
```

Both will never recover (Clave doesn't implement NIP-42 AUTH; garden.zap.cooking has been 502 for months). They sit in the pool because old `clients.json` entries still reference them in their URI relay sets, and the current code retries indefinitely.

## How it works

- New per-entry counter `successfulOpens` (incremented when WS reaches `open` state)
- New per-entry flag `evicted: false`
- On `close`: after `failures++`, if `failures >= maxFailuresWithoutSuccess && successfulOpens === 0 && !evicted`, mark `evicted: true`, log a warning, and skip `scheduleReconnect`
- `addRelay` on an existing evicted entry: bumps `refCount` but doesn't reopen
- `releaseRelay` on evicted entry: normal flow — when refCount hits 0, entry is removed from the pool
- A future `addRelay` after deletion creates a brand-new un-evicted entry that retries from scratch — so eviction is per-(entry-lifetime), not per-process-lifetime

`successfulOpens === 0` (not `successfulEvents === 0`) is the right criterion — it distinguishes permanently broken relays (403/502 never reach `open`) from healthy-but-quiet relays (open fine, just nobody is signing on them right now).

Default threshold: 10. With the standard backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, …, capped at 600s), 10 failures takes ~17 minutes — long enough to ride out a real outage, short enough to stop wasting resources on a permanent dead relay. Configurable via constructor.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test relay-proxy/test/relayPool.test.js` — 22/22 pass (4 new cases)
- [x] `node --test relay-proxy/test/` — full 79/79 proxy suite pass
- [ ] Deploy to Dell: `sudo cp relay-proxy/relayPool.js /opt/clave-proxy/ && sudo systemctl restart clave-proxy`
- [ ] Verify post-deploy via `sudo journalctl -u clave-proxy --since "30 min ago" | grep -E "permanently failed|RelayPool"` — expect:
  - within ~17 min, both `nostr.wine` and `garden.zap.cooking/` get a one-time `permanently failed after N attempts (no successful opens) — releasing` line
  - no further reconnect attempts logged for those URLs
  - other healthy relays in pool (powr.build, nos.lol, damus.io, primal.net, bucket.coracle.social, ephemeral.snowflare.cc, relay.nsec.app) keep their reconnect/heartbeat behavior unchanged

## Closes
